title.en: Volume 425 Biographies 184: Liu Yinglong, Pan 牥, Hong Qin, Zhao Jingwei, Feng Qufei, Xu Lin, Xu Zongren, Wei Zhaode, Chen Kai, Yang Wenzhong, Xie Fangde
title.raw: 卷四百二十五 列傳第一百八十四 劉應龍 潘牥 洪芹 趙景緯 馮去非 徐霖 徐宗仁 危昭德 陳塏 楊文仲 謝枋得 Volume 425 Biographies 184: Liu Yinglong, Pan 牥, Hong Qin, Zhao Jingwei, Feng Qufei, Xu Lin, Xu Zongren, Wei Zhaode, Chen Kai, Yang Wenzhong, Xie Fangde

sentences.zh: 劉應龍潘方洪芹趙景緯馮去非徐霖徐宗仁危昭德陳塏楊文仲謝枋得

translations.literal: Liu Yinglong, Pan Fang, Hong Qin, Zhao Jingwei, Feng Qufei, Xu Lin, Xu Zongren, Wei Zhaode, Chen Kai, Yang Wenzhong, Xie Fangde
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yinglong, Pan Fang, Hong Qin, Zhao Jingwei, Feng Qufei, Xu Lin, Xu Zongren, Wei Zhaode, Chen Kai, Yang Wenzhong, and Xie Fangde

sentences.zh: 劉應龍，字漢臣，瑞州高安人。

translations.literal: Liu Yinglong, courtesy name Hanchen, was a native of Gao'an in Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yinglong, styled Hanchen, came from Gao'an in Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaxi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1238.

sentences.zh: 授零陵主簿，饒州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Registrar of Lingling and Judicial Assistant of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made registrar of Lingling and judicial assistant in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 有毛隆者，務剽掠殺人，州民被盜，遙呼盜曰：“汝毛隆也？

translations.literal: There was a Mao Long who devoted himself to plundering and killing people. When the people of the prefecture suffered robbery, they would call out to the thief from afar, "Are you Mao Long?"
translations.idiomatic: A man named Mao Long made a career of plunder and murder. When locals were robbed, they would shout at the thief from a distance, "Are you Mao Long?"

sentences.zh: ”盜亦曰：“我毛隆也。

translations.literal: The thief would also say, "I am Mao Long."
translations.idiomatic: The thief would answer, "Yes — I am Mao Long."

sentences.zh: ”既，訟於官，捕隆置獄，應龍曰：“盜誠毛隆，其肯自謂？

translations.literal: Afterwards, when the case was brought to court, Long was arrested and placed in prison. Yinglong said, "If the thief were truly Mao Long, would he acknowledge it himself?"
translations.idiomatic: Later the matter went to court, Mao Long was arrested and jailed. Yinglong said, "If the bandit really were Mao Long, would he admit to it?"

sentences.zh: ”因言於州，州不可，乃委它官，隆誣伏抵死，未幾盜敗，應龍繇是著名。

translations.literal: He therefore spoke to the prefecture, but the prefecture would not accept it and entrusted the case to another official. Long falsely confessed and was executed. Before long the real thief was caught, and from this Yinglong became famous.
translations.idiomatic: He argued his point to the prefectural authorities, but they would not listen and handed the case to another judge. Long was induced to confess falsely and was put to death. Not long after, the real bandit was caught, and Yinglong won renown for this.

sentences.zh: 改知崇仁縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Chongren County.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as magistrate of Chongren County.

sentences.zh: 淮西失守，江西諸州有殘破者，縣佐貳聞變先遁，應龍固守不去。

translations.literal: When Huai West was lost, several prefectures in Jiangxi were ravaged. The county assistants and deputies fled at the first news of trouble, but Yinglong held firm and did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai West fell, several prefectures in Jiangxi were laid waste. The county's deputies fled at the first alarm, but Yinglong held his post and refused to abandon it.

sentences.zh: 先是，理宗久未有子，以弟福王與芮之子為皇子，丞相吳潛有異論，帝已不樂。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Lizong had long been without a son and had made the son of his younger brother, Prince Fu Yunrui, crown prince. The Chief Councillor Wu Qian held a dissenting view, and the Emperor was already displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Lizong had long been without an heir and had named the son of his younger brother, Prince Fu Yunrui, as crown prince. Chief Councillor Wu Qian had voiced objections, and the Emperor was already displeased with him.

sentences.zh: 大元兵度江，朝野震動，逐丞相丁大全，復起潛為相，帝問潛策安出，潛對曰：“當遷幸。

translations.literal: When the Great Yuan army crossed the Yangzi, court and commoners were shaken. Chief Councillor Ding Daquan was dismissed and Qian was restored as chief councillor. The Emperor asked where Qian's plan lay. Qian replied, "Your Majesty should move the capital."
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan army crossed the Yangzi, the court and the people were thrown into turmoil. Chief Councillor Ding Daquan was dismissed and Wu Qian was recalled to office. The Emperor asked what plan Wu Qian proposed. Wu Qian answered, "Your Majesty should relocate the court."

sentences.zh: ”又問卿如何，潛曰：“臣當死守於此。

translations.literal: The Emperor then asked what Qian himself would do. Qian said, "Your servant will die defending this place."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then asked what he himself intended to do. Wu Qian said, "I shall die defending this place."

sentences.zh: ”帝泣下曰：“卿欲為張邦昌乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor wept and said, "Do you wish to become another Zhang Bangchang?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept and said, "Do you mean to play Zhang Bangchang to me?"

sentences.zh: ”潛不敢復言。

translations.literal: Qian did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qian dared say no more.

sentences.zh: 未幾北兵退，帝語群臣曰：“吳潛幾誤朕。

translations.literal: Before long the northern army withdrew. The Emperor told the assembled ministers, "Wu Qian nearly misled Us."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the northern armies withdrew. The Emperor told his ministers, "Wu Qian nearly led me astray."

sentences.zh: ”遂罷潛相。

translations.literal: Qian was then dismissed from the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qian was thereupon removed from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 帝怒潛不已，應龍朝受命，帝夜出象簡書疏稿授應龍，使劾潛，應龍謂：“潛本有賢譽，獨論事失當，臨變寡斷。

translations.literal: The Emperor's anger at Qian did not cease. Yinglong received his court appointment; that night the Emperor brought out an ivory tally and handed him the draft of a memorial, ordering him to impeach Qian. Yinglong said, "Qian originally enjoyed a reputation for worthiness; he erred only in his policy proposals and showed little resolve in a crisis."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's anger at Wu Qian did not abate. After Yinglong took up his court appointment, the Emperor came out at night with an ivory tally and handed him the draft of a memorial, instructing him to impeach Wu Qian. Yinglong said, "Wu Qian has long enjoyed a reputation for talent; he merely chose the wrong course in debate and showed little resolve when crisis came."

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來，大臣有罪未嘗輕肆誅戮。

translations.literal: Since the founding ancestors, when great ministers were guilty, execution had never been lightly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the dynasty, guilty ministers had never been put to death lightly.

sentences.zh: 欲望姑從寬典，以全體貌。

translations.literal: I wish that for the moment lenient treatment may be applied, so as to preserve his person intact.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that for now he be treated with leniency, so that his person and standing may be preserved.

sentences.zh: ”帝大怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 乃按劾丁大全，請加竄斥，疏言：“內莫急於蘇民瘼以固國本，外莫急於討軍實以振國威。

translations.literal: He then investigated and impeached Ding Daquan, requesting that he be further banished and exiled. In his memorial he said, "Within, nothing is more urgent than relieving the people's distress to strengthen the foundation of the state; without, nothing is more urgent than building up military strength to restore national prestige."
translations.idiomatic: He then brought charges against Ding Daquan and asked that he be banished still farther. In his memorial he wrote, "Domestically, nothing is more urgent than easing the people's suffering to shore up the foundations of the state; abroad, nothing is more urgent than building up military strength to restore national prestige."

sentences.zh: ”又言時政四事，廣發稟以振民饑，通商販以助民食，勸分富室以助官糴，嚴等第以核民數，稽檢放以蘇民窮，嚴戢盜以除民害。

translations.literal: He also spoke of four matters of current policy: broadly issuing grain from the granaries to relieve famine among the people; opening trade to aid the people's food supply; encouraging wealthy households to share grain to assist official purchases; strictly grading households to verify population registers; examining relief distributions to revive the destitute; and strictly suppressing bandits to remove harm from the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also set forth four policy measures: issue grain widely from the public granaries to relieve famine; open commerce to supplement the people's food supply; urge wealthy households to share grain for official purchases; enforce strict household grading to verify population registers; audit relief distributions to rescue the destitute; and crack down firmly on banditry to remove a scourge upon the people.

sentences.zh: 賈似道素忌潛，會京師米貴，應龍為《勸糶歌》宦者取以上聞，帝問知應龍所作，問似道米價高，當亟處之，似道訪其由，亦怒應龍。

translations.literal: Jia Sidao had long resented Qian. It happened that rice in the capital was dear. Yinglong composed a "Song Urging the Sale of Grain." A eunuch took it and reported it upward. The Emperor asked and learned that Yinglong had written it. He asked Sidao why rice prices were high and said it should be dealt with at once. Sidao inquired into the cause and was also angry at Yinglong.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao had long borne a grudge against Wu Qian. At the time rice in the capital was costly, and Yinglong composed a "Song Urging the Sale of Grain." A eunuch brought it to the Emperor's attention. When the Emperor learned that Yinglong had written it, he asked Sidao why rice prices were so high and said the matter must be addressed immediately. Sidao traced the source and grew angry at Yinglong as well.

sentences.zh: 遷司農少卿，尋以右諫議大夫孫附鳳言，遂去國。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, but soon, on the word of Sun Fufeng, Right Remonstrating Censor, he left the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, but soon, on a memorial from Sun Fufeng, Right Remonstrating Censor, he left the capital.

sentences.zh: 景定三年，湖南饑，起提舉常平。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingding, when Hunan suffered famine, he was recalled to serve as Intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1262, when Hunan was stricken by famine, he was recalled as Intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 以救荒功，遷直寶章閣、廣南東路轉運判官。

translations.literal: For his merit in famine relief he was promoted to Direct Accessory at the Baozhang Pavilion and Transport Assessor of the Eastern Circuit of Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: For his work in famine relief he was made Direct Accessory at the Baozhang Pavilion and Transport Assessor for the Eastern Circuit of Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監兼國史編修、實錄檢討。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Library, concurrently Compiler of the National History and Reviser of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Library, with concurrent duties as Compiler of the National History and Reviser of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 知隆興府兼江西轉運副使，奏免和糴二十萬石。

translations.literal: As Prefect of Longxing and concurrent Vice Transport Commissioner of Jiangxi, he memorialized to exempt two hundred thousand piculs of compulsory grain purchases.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Longxing and concurrent Vice Transport Commissioner of Jiangxi, he memorialized to exempt two hundred thousand piculs of compulsory grain purchases.

sentences.zh: 擢權戶部侍郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Acting Vice Minister of Revenue, concurrently Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Vice Minister of Revenue and Court Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 時似道當國，百官奏對稍切直者輒黜，應龍言：“臣觀今日之事，可言者多矣。

translations.literal: At that time Sidao held power. Whenever an official who spoke somewhat frankly in audience was dismissed, Yinglong said, "Your servant observes that in affairs today there is much that may be spoken of."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sidao held the reins of government. Officials who spoke even moderately frankly in audience were dismissed one after another. Yinglong said, "I see that in the affairs of today there is a great deal that ought to be said."

sentences.zh: 邇日以來，靖恭自守者以論事為忌，指陳稍切者聯翩引去，豈兩省繳駁過甚，重其疑歟？

translations.literal: In recent days those who kept themselves respectful and reserved took discussion of affairs as taboo; those whose remonstrances were somewhat pointed were dismissed in succession. Is it because the Two Departments' rebuttals were excessive and their suspicions weighed too heavily?
translations.idiomatic: Lately those who kept their heads down have treated speaking on policy as forbidden, while those whose remonstrances were even slightly pointed have been dismissed in quick succession. Is it because the Two Departments' rebuttals have been too severe and their suspicions too heavy?

sentences.zh: 抑廷臣奏對咈意，速其畏歟？

translations.literal: Or is it that when court ministers spoke in audience contrary to the Emperor's intent, they were swiftly made to fear?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it that when court ministers spoke against the Emperor's wishes in audience, they were swiftly made to fear for their positions?

sentences.zh: 朝廷清明之時，而言者已懷疑畏，臣恐正臣奪氣，鯁臣吃舌，宜非盛世所有。

translations.literal: In a time when the court was clear and bright, those who spoke already harbored suspicion and fear. Your servant fears that upright ministers would lose their spirit and blunt ministers would bite their tongues — this ought not to belong to an age of flourishing governance.
translations.idiomatic: In an age when the court was supposed to be enlightened, those who spoke already nursed suspicion and fear. I fear that upright ministers will lose heart and blunt-spoken ministers will bite their tongues — surely this is not what a flourishing age should look like.

sentences.zh: ”遂迕當路，自侍從、兩省以下無不切齒。

translations.literal: He thereby offended those in power. From the attendant ministers and the Two Departments downward, none did not gnash their teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby offended those in power, and from the attendant ministers and the Two Departments on down, all gnashed their teeth at him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以集英殿修撰知建寧府，亟辭，中書舍人盧鉞希指封還錄黃。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Compiler at the Jiying Hall and Prefect of Jianning, but he urgently declined. Lu Yue, Drafting Attendant of the Central Secretariat, reading the court's wishes, returned the sealed draft.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Compiler at the Jiying Hall and prefect of Jianning, but he urgently declined. Lu Yue, Drafting Attendant of the Central Secretariat, reading the court's wishes, returned the sealed appointment draft.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為江東轉運使，辭。

translations.literal: After a long while he was recalled as Transport Commissioner of Jiangdong, but he declined.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled as Transport Commissioner of Jiangdong, but again he declined.

sentences.zh: 南海寇作，朝廷患之，乃以顯謨閣待制知廣州、廣東紗略安撫使。

translations.literal: Bandits arose in the Southern Sea and the court was troubled. He was therefore made Awaiting Draft at the Xianmo Pavilion, Prefect of Guangzhou, and Pacification Commissioner for Guangdong Yarn and Tax.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates rose in the Southern Sea the court was alarmed and appointed him Awaiting Draft at the Xianmo Pavilion, prefect of Guangzhou, and Pacification Commissioner for Guangdong Yarn and Tax.

sentences.zh: 寇聞應龍至，遁去。

translations.literal: When the bandits heard that Yinglong had arrived, they fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates heard that Yinglong had arrived, they fled.

sentences.zh: 應龍剿逐之，南海大治。

translations.literal: Yinglong pursued and drove them off, and the Southern Sea was greatly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong pursued and drove them off, and the Southern Sea was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 特旨屢召，拜戶部侍郎仍兼侍讀，七上奏辭免。

translations.literal: By special edict he was repeatedly summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, still concurrently Court Reader. Seven times he memorialized to decline.
translations.idiomatic: By special edict he was repeatedly summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, still concurrently Court Reader. Seven times he memorialized to decline.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，遷兵部尚書、寶章閣直學士、知贛州，兼江西兵馬鈐轄、青海軍節度使，力辭，隱九峰。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou he was transferred to Minister of War, Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, and Prefect of Ganzhou, concurrently Military Controller of Jiangxi and Military Commissioner of the Qinghai Army. He strenuously declined and retired to seclusion on Jiufeng.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 he was made Minister of War, Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, and prefect of Ganzhou, with concurrent duties as Military Controller of Jiangxi and Military Commissioner of the Qinghai Army. He strenuously declined and withdrew to seclusion on Mount Jiufeng.

sentences.zh: 子元高亦舉進士，知候官縣。

translations.literal: His son Yuangao also passed the jinshi examination and served as magistrate of Houguan County.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuangao also received the jinshi degree and served as magistrate of Houguan County.

sentences.zh: 沒，洪天錫嘆曰：“朝廷失一御史矣。

translations.literal: When he died, Hong Tiansi sighed and said, "The court has lost a censor."
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Hong Tiansi sighed and said, "The court has lost a censor."

sentences.zh: 潘方字庭堅，福州閩人。

translations.literal: Pan Fang, courtesy name Tingjian, was a native of Min in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Fang, styled Tingjian, came from Min in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 端平二年策進士，方對曰：“陛下承休上帝，皈德匹夫，何異為人子孫，身荷父母劬勞之賜，乃指豪奴悍婢為恩私之地。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duanping he passed the policy examination for jinshi. In his audience Fang replied, "Your Majesty inherits repose from the Supreme Emperor and returns virtue to common men — how is this different from being someone's descendant, personally bearing the toil and favor of parents, yet pointing to overbearing servants and fierce maidservants as the ground of private favor?"
translations.idiomatic: In 1235 he passed the policy examination for jinshi. In his audience Fang said, "Your Majesty inherits repose from Heaven above and returns virtue to the common people — yet how is this different from a son who owes his parents a lifetime of labor and care, only to treat overbearing servants and fierce maidservants as the source of private favor?"

sentences.zh: 欲父母無怒，不可得也。

translations.literal: To wish that parents be without anger — this cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish your parents to remain free of anger, that cannot be achieved.

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“陛下手足之愛，生榮死哀，反不得視士庶人。

translations.literal: He also said, "Your Majesty's love for a brother — honored in life and mourned in death — yet he may not even be regarded as common gentry and commoners."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Your Majesty's love for a brother — honored in life and mourned in death — yet he may not even receive the regard accorded ordinary subjects."

sentences.zh: 此如一門之內，骨肉之間未能親睦，是以僮仆疾視，鄰裏生侮。

translations.literal: This is like within a single household, where flesh and bone cannot be intimate and harmonious — therefore servants look on with hostility and neighbors give rise to contempt.
translations.idiomatic: This is like a household in which kin cannot live in harmony — so that servants look on with hostility and neighbors take it as license for contempt.

sentences.zh: 宜厚東海之恩，裂淮南之土，以致人和。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should thicken the grace shown to the Eastern Sea and divide the lands of Huainan, so as to bring about harmony among men.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should show greater favor to the prince of the Eastern Sea and grant him lands in Huainan, so as to restore harmony among men.

sentences.zh: ”時對者數百人，庭堅語最直。

translations.literal: At that time several hundred men answered in audience, but Tingjian's words were the most direct.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred candidates answered in audience that day, but Tingjian's words were the most forthright.

sentences.zh: 會殿中侍御史蔣峴劾方大琮、劉克莊、王邁前倡異論，並誣方姓同逆賊，策語不順，請皆論以漢法。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Attendant Censor Jiang Xian impeached Fang Dacong, Liu Kezhuang, and Wang Mai for having earlier advocated heterodox views, and also falsely charged that the surname Fang was the same as that of a rebel bandit and that Fang's policy language was disloyal, requesting that all be judged by Han law.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Palace Attendant Censor Jiang Xian impeached Fang Dacong, Liu Kezhuang, and Wang Mai for having earlier advocated heterodox views, and also falsely charged that Pan's surname matched that of a rebel bandit and that his policy language was disloyal, requesting that all be punished under Han law.

sentences.zh: 方調鎮南軍節度推官、衢州推官，歷浙西提舉常平司。

translations.literal: Fang was transferred to serve as Investigating Officer of the Zhennan Army Military Commission and Investigating Officer of Quzhou, and served in the Zhexi Intendancy of the Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Pan was transferred to serve as investigating officer of the Zhennan Army Military Commission and of Quzhou, and later served in the Zhexi Intendancy of the Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 遷太學正，旬日，出通判潭州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Imperial College. Within ten days he was sent out as Vice Prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Imperial College, and within ten days was sent out as vice prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 日食，應詔上封事曰：“熙寧初元日食，詔郡縣掩骼，著為令。

translations.literal: When an eclipse occurred, by imperial order he submitted a sealed memorial saying, "In the first year of Xining, when an eclipse occurred, an edict ordered prefectures and counties to bury exposed bones, and this was established as a regulation."
translations.idiomatic: When a solar eclipse occurred, by imperial order he submitted a sealed memorial saying, "In the first year of the Xining reign, when an eclipse occurred, an edict ordered prefectures and counties to bury exposed bones, and this was established as a permanent regulation."

sentences.zh: 故王一扌不淺土，其為暴骸亦大矣。

translations.literal: Yet the former king was buried in a shallow handful of earth — how great a number of exposed corpses this represents as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the former king lies buried under only a shallow handful of earth — how many exposed corpses does this represent as well.

sentences.zh: 請以王禮改葬。

translations.literal: I request that he be reburied according to the rites due a king.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be reburied according to the rites due a king.

sentences.zh: ”又移書丞相遊似申言之，似心善其言，方將收用之，而方卒。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Chief Councillor You Si stating this. Si was inwardly pleased with his words and was about to bring Fang into employment, but Fang died.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Chief Councillor You Si to make the same point. You Si was inwardly pleased with his argument and was about to bring Pan into service, but Pan died.

sentences.zh: 洪芹，尚書右仆射適之曾孫，以大父澤入官，甫更調，登進士第。

translations.literal: Hong Qin was the great-grandson of Hong Shi, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. Through his grandfather Ze he entered office; after only one transfer he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Qin was the great-grandson of Hong Shi, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. Through his grandfather Ze he entered office; after only one transfer he received the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 自南平司法改欽州教授。

translations.literal: From Judicial Assistant of Nanping he was transferred to Professor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From judicial assistant of Nanping he was transferred to professor in Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 部使者愛其才，先後並薦之，有旨召審察。

translations.literal: The circuit envoy admired his talent and recommended him on successive occasions. An edict ordered that he be summoned for examination.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit envoy admired his talent and recommended him repeatedly. An edict ordered that he be summoned for examination.

sentences.zh: 丁內外艱。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He observed mourning for his parents.

sentences.zh: 入主省架閣，遷太學博士。

translations.literal: He entered the Secretariat as Archivist and was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Secretariat as archivist and was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 輪對，發明絜矩之道。

translations.literal: In rotation audience he expounded the Way of the Carpenter's Square.
translations.idiomatic: In rotation audience he expounded the principle of the carpenter's square — the standard of measured conduct.

sentences.zh: 擢國子博士，出通判南劍，入為太常博士，累遷將作少監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Erudite of the Directorate of Education, sent out as Vice Prefect of Nanjian, recalled as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Erudite of the Directorate of Education, sent out as vice prefect of Nanjian, recalled as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and eventually rose to Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 屬詞臣無當上意，慨然思得天下士，丞相程元鳳言當今地望無逾洪芹者，進兼翰林，權直秘書少監。

translations.literal: It happened that the literary officials did not suit the Emperor's intent. He sighed and wished to obtain men of talent throughout the realm. Chief Councillor Cheng Yuanfeng said that in present reputation and standing none surpassed Hong Qin. He was advanced to concurrent service in the Hanlin Academy and Acting Direct Accessory of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the literary officials failed to satisfy the Emperor's wishes. He sighed and wished to find men of talent throughout the realm. Chief Councillor Cheng Yuanfeng said that in present reputation and standing none surpassed Hong Qin. He was advanced to concurrent service in the Hanlin Academy and Acting Direct Accessory of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎，帝銳意向用而以論去，退寓永嘉，怡然自適。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites. The Emperor was keen to employ him, but because of criticism he left office, retired to lodge at Yongjia, and was content and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites. The Emperor was keen to employ him, but because of criticism he left office, retired to Yongjia, and lived contentedly.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳初，起知寧國府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianchun he was recalled to serve as Prefect of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xianchun reign he was recalled as prefect of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 有文集。

translations.literal: He left a collected literary works.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected literary works.

sentences.zh: 趙景緯字德父，臨安府於潛人。

translations.literal: Zhao Jingwei, courtesy name Defu, was a native of Yuqian in Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jingwei, styled Defu, came from Yuqian in Lin'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少勤學，弱冠得周惇頤、程顥兄弟諸書讀之，恨不及登朱熹之門。

translations.literal: In youth he studied diligently. At twenty he obtained the works of Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers to read, and regretted that he had not been able to enter Zhu Xi's school.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied diligently. At twenty he obtained the works of Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers and read them with devotion, regretting that he had never been able to study under Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 熹門人葉味道謂之曰：“度正，吾黨中第一人。

translations.literal: Ye Weidao, a disciple of Xi, said to him, "Du Zheng is the foremost man in our fellowship."
translations.idiomatic: Ye Weidao, a disciple of Zhu Xi, told him, "Du Zheng is the foremost man in our fellowship."

sentences.zh: ”遂往見，首誨以求放心為本。

translations.literal: He thereupon went to see him. At the outset he was taught that seeking to recover the lost mind was fundamental.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon went to see Du Zheng, who at the outset taught him that recovering the lost mind was fundamental.

sentences.zh: 由是往來味道、正之間，研索益精。

translations.literal: From this he went back and forth between Weidao and Zheng, and his investigation and inquiry grew ever more refined.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he moved between Ye Weidao and Du Zheng, and his inquiry grew ever more refined.

sentences.zh: 入太學，登淳祐元年進士第。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial College and passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Chunyou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial College and received his jinshi degree in 1241.

sentences.zh: 授江陰軍教授，諸生守其榘度。

translations.literal: He was appointed Professor of Jiangyin Prefecture, and the students observed his rules and measures.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed professor at Jiangyin, and his students observed his standards of conduct.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，以祿不逮養，服闋不調。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother. Because his salary had not sufficed to support her, when mourning ended he did not take up a new appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he observed mourning. Because his salary had never been enough to support her properly, when mourning ended he did not accept a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 作《讀易庵懸霤山》。

translations.literal: He composed "Reading the Changes Hermitage on Xuansao Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "Reading the Changes Hermitage on Xuansao Mountain."

sentences.zh: 江東提點刑獄吳勢卿辟為幹辦公事，不就。

translations.literal: Wu Shiqing, Judicial Intendant of Jiangdong, invited him to serve as Administrative Aide, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiqing, Judicial Intendant of Jiangdong, invited him to serve as administrative aide, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 召為史館檢閱，辭，不許；

translations.literal: He was summoned as Reviewer of the History Institute, but declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Reviewer of the History Institute and declined, but the court would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 乞換待次教授，不許；

translations.literal: He requested to be exchanged for a professor awaiting assignment; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be exchanged for a professor awaiting assignment; this too was refused.

sentences.zh: 乞嶽祠，又不許；

translations.literal: He requested a mountain shrine post; again this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a mountain shrine post; again the court refused.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕，不報。

translations.literal: He requested retirement; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire; no answer came.

sentences.zh: 有旨特與改合入官，主管崇道觀，三辭，不許。

translations.literal: An edict specially granted him conversion to a regular-rank office and appointment as Superintendent of the Chongdao Abbey. Three times he declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially converted him to regular rank and appointed him superintendent of the Chongdao Abbey. Three times he declined; each time the court refused.

sentences.zh: 景定元年，特授秘書郎，兩辭，不許。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingding he was specially appointed Secretary; twice he declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1260 he was specially appointed Secretary; twice he declined; each time the court refused.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎，辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Compiler; he declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Compiler and declined; again the court refused.

sentences.zh: 以疾丐祠，差主管佑神觀兼史館校勘。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested a shrine post and was assigned Superintendent of the Youshen Abbey, concurrently Collator of the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: On grounds of illness he asked for a shrine post and was assigned superintendent of the Youshen Abbey, with concurrent duties as collator of the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 史成，兩乞外祠，進直秘閣，與在外宮觀，辭職名，不許。

translations.literal: When the history was completed, twice he requested an outside shrine post. He was advanced to Direct Accessory of the Secret Vault and granted an outside palace abbey, but he declined the title; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the history was completed, twice he asked for an outside shrine post. He was advanced to Direct Accessory of the Secret Vault and granted an outside palace abbey, but declined the title; the court would not accept.

sentences.zh: 差主管崇禧觀。

translations.literal: He was assigned Superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 臺州守王華甫建上蔡書院，禮景緯為堂長，以疾辭。

translations.literal: Wang Huafu, Prefect of Taizhou, built the Shangcai Academy and honored Jingwei as hall director, but he declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huafu, prefect of Taizhou, built the Shangcai Academy and invited Jingwei to serve as hall director, but he declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 依舊職差知臺州，兩辭，不許，趣命益嚴。

translations.literal: According to his former office he was assigned to know Taizhou. Twice he declined; this was not permitted, and the urgent orders grew ever stricter.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to his former post as prefect of Taizhou. Twice he declined; the court refused, and the urgent orders grew ever more insistent.

sentences.zh: 至郡，以化民成俗為先務，首取陳述古《諭俗文》書示諸邑，且自為之說，使其民更相告諭、諷誦、服行，期無失墜。

translations.literal: When he reached the prefecture, he made transforming the people and completing customs his first task. He first took Chen Shugu's "Admonitory Essay on Customs," had it written out and shown to all districts, and himself provided exposition, causing the people to admonish one another, chant and recite it, and practice it, expecting that nothing would be lost or neglected.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the prefecture, he made transforming the people and reforming local customs his first priority. He took Chen Shugu's "Admonitory Essay on Customs," had copies distributed to every district, and wrote his own commentary, urging the people to admonish one another, chant the text, and put it into practice, so that nothing would be neglected.

sentences.zh: 約束官吏擾民五事。

translations.literal: He imposed restrictions on five matters in which officials harassed the people.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed restrictions on five ways in which officials harassed the people.

sentences.zh: 取《孝經庶人章》為四言詠贊其義，使朝夕歌之，至有為之感涕者。

translations.literal: He took the "Commoners' Chapter" of the Classic of Filial Piety and made a four-character chant praising its meaning, causing the people to sing it morning and evening, until some were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: He took the "Commoners' Chapter" of the Classic of Filial Piety and composed a four-character chant praising its meaning, which the people sang morning and evening until some were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 舉遺逸車若水、林正心於朝。

translations.literal: He recommended to the court the reclusive scholars Che Ruoshui and Lin Zhengxin.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended the reclusive scholars Che Ruoshui and Lin Zhengxin to the court.

sentences.zh: 旌孝行，作《訓孝文》以勵其俗。

translations.literal: He honored filial conduct and composed "An Admonition on Filial Piety" to encourage local custom.
translations.idiomatic: He honored filial conduct and wrote "An Admonition on Filial Piety" to encourage local custom.

sentences.zh: 平重刑，懲嘩訐，治豪橫。

translations.literal: He lightened heavy punishments, punished clamor and denunciation, and dealt with overbearing local bullies.
translations.idiomatic: He lightened heavy punishments, punished clamorous denunciation, and cracked down on local bullies.

sentences.zh: 建黃巖縣社倉六十有六。

translations.literal: He built sixty-six community granaries in Huangyan County.
translations.idiomatic: He built sixty-six community granaries in Huangyan County.

sentences.zh: 浚河道九十里，築堤路三十里。

translations.literal: He dredged river channels for ninety li and built embankment roads for thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged ninety li of waterways and built thirty li of embankment roads.

sentences.zh: 節浮費，為下戶代輸秋苗。

translations.literal: He restrained extravagant expenditures and paid autumn grain tax on behalf of lower households.
translations.idiomatic: He cut wasteful spending and paid autumn grain tax on behalf of poorer households.

sentences.zh: 奏蠲五邑坊河渡錢。

translations.literal: He memorialized to remit ferry tolls at ward river crossings in five districts.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to remit ferry tolls at ward river crossings in five districts.

sentences.zh: 斯年之內，乞歸田裏者再。

translations.literal: Within that year he twice requested to return to his fields and village.
translations.idiomatic: Within that year he twice asked to return to private life.

sentences.zh: 進考功郎官，再辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Director of the Bureau of Personnel Evaluation. Twice he declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Personnel Evaluation. Twice he declined; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 兼沂靖惠王府教授，辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was concurrently appointed Professor of the Yijinghui Princely Establishment. He declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently appointed professor of the Yijinghui Princely Establishment. He declined; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 是冬，四辭新命，且乞祠，皆不許。

translations.literal: That winter he four times declined new appointments and also requested a shrine post; none of this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he four times declined new appointments and also asked for a shrine post; each time the court refused.

sentences.zh: 乃乞於赤城、桐柏之間采藥著書，庶幾有補後學，使病廢之身不為無用於聖世，不許。

translations.literal: He then requested to gather herbs and write books between Chicheng and Tongbai, hoping thereby to benefit later students and cause his sick and disabled person not to be useless to the sagely age. This was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to gather herbs and write books between Mount Chicheng and Mount Tongbai, hoping thereby to benefit later students and make his sick, disabled body of some use to the age. The court refused.

sentences.zh: 御筆兼崇政殿說書，三辭，不許。

translations.literal: By the Emperor's own brush he was concurrently made Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall. Three times he declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: By the Emperor's own hand he was concurrently made Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall. Three times he declined; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 乃造朝，侍緝熙殿，以《易》進講，論“聖人體元之妙在惟幾，人君得此，則天下有治而無亂，人事有吉而無兇矣”。

translations.literal: He then came to court, attended at the Jixi Hall, and lectured on the Changes, discussing how "the subtlety of the sage's embodiment of the Origin lies in discerning the incipient; when the ruler obtains this, then the realm has order without disorder and human affairs have auspice without misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: He then came to court, lectured at the Jixi Hall on the Changes, and explained that "the sage's embodiment of the Origin lies in discerning subtle signs at their inception; when a ruler grasps this, the realm will know order without disorder and human affairs will know fortune without misfortune."

sentences.zh: 又曰：“惕厲祗懼，乃天心之所存。

translations.literal: He also said, "Vigilance, discipline, reverence, and fear — these are what the mind of Heaven preserves."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Vigilance, discipline, reverence, and fear are what Heaven's mind preserves."

sentences.zh: 聖人先處於憂，故能無憂，先處以危，故能無危；

translations.literal: The sage first places himself in worry, and therefore can be without worry; first places himself in danger, and therefore can be without danger.
translations.idiomatic: The sage first places himself in worry and therefore remains free of worry; first places himself in danger and therefore remains free of danger.

sentences.zh: 若乃先自處於安樂，則憂危乘之矣。

translations.literal: If one first places oneself in ease and pleasure, then worry and danger will ride upon it.
translations.idiomatic: But if one first settles into ease and pleasure, worry and danger will soon overtake one.

sentences.zh: ”又論監司守令，其說曰：“知人之難，自古已然。

translations.literal: He also discussed circuit intendants and prefectural magistrates. His argument said, "The difficulty of knowing men has been so since antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke on circuit intendants and prefectural magistrates, saying, "The difficulty of knowing men has been so since antiquity."

sentences.zh: 人才乏使，莫今為甚。

translations.literal: Talented men are lacking for employment — never has this been worse than today.
translations.idiomatic: Talented men are scarce for appointment — never has the shortage been worse than today.

sentences.zh: 或觀望而撓於勢，或阿私而徇於情，或是非不公而以枉為直，或毀譽失實而以汙為廉。

translations.literal: Some waver in observation and yield to power; some flatter private interests and follow personal feelings; some are unjust in right and wrong and take the crooked for straight; some lose truth in praise and blame and take the filthy for pure.
translations.idiomatic: Some waver and yield to power; some flatter private interests and follow personal feelings; some distort right and wrong and call the crooked straight; some falsify praise and blame and call the corrupt honest.

sentences.zh: 遂使舉刺不當，不足以服天下之心。

translations.literal: Thus recommendations and impeachments are improper and insufficient to win the hearts of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Thus recommendations and impeachments are improper and fail to win the hearts of the realm.

sentences.zh: 與其糾劾於有罪之後，而未必盡得其情；

translations.literal: Rather than impeach after guilt has occurred, yet not necessarily obtain the full truth of the matter;
translations.idiomatic: Rather than impeach after guilt has already occurred, yet fail to grasp the full truth of the matter,

sentences.zh: 孰若精擇於未用之先，而使之各稱其職。

translations.literal: would it not be better to select with care before men are employed, and cause each to fulfill his office?
translations.idiomatic: would it not be better to select with care before men are employed, so that each may fulfill his proper office?

sentences.zh: 彗出於柳，景緯應詔上封事曰：

translations.literal: A comet appeared in the Willow mansion. By imperial order Jingwei submitted a sealed memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared in the Willow mansion, Jingwei submitted a sealed memorial by imperial order, saying:

sentences.zh: 今日求所以解天意者，不過悅人心而已。

translations.literal: Today in seeking how to interpret the mind of Heaven, nothing goes beyond pleasing the minds of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Today, in seeking how to interpret Heaven's will, nothing goes beyond pleasing the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 百姓之心即天心也。

translations.literal: The mind of the common people is the mind of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The people's hearts are Heaven's heart.

sentences.zh: 錮私藏而專天下之同欲，則人不悅。

translations.literal: If private hoards are locked up and the shared desires of all under Heaven are monopolized, then the people are not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: If private hoards are locked away and the shared desires of the realm are monopolized, the people will not be pleased.

sentences.zh: 保私人而違天下之公議，則人不悅。

translations.literal: If private persons are protected and the public consensus of all under Heaven is violated, then the people are not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: If private favorites are protected and the public consensus of the realm is violated, the people will not be pleased.

sentences.zh: 閭閻之糟糠不厭，而燕私之供奉自如，則人不悅。

translations.literal: If the coarse grain of lanes and alleys is never enough, yet private banquets are supplied as before, then the people are not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: If the people in the lanes cannot get enough coarse grain to eat, yet private banquets continue as before, the people will not be pleased.

sentences.zh: 百姓之膏血日朘，而符移之星火愈急，則人不悅。

translations.literal: If the people's fat and blood are daily drained, while official documents fly like sparks ever more urgently, then the people are not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: If the people's substance is drained daily while official demands fly like sparks ever more urgently, the people will not be pleased.

sentences.zh: 不公於己而欲絕天下之私，則人不悅。

translations.literal: If one is not fair to oneself yet wishes to cut off all private interest under Heaven, then the people are not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: If the court is not fair in its own conduct yet wishes to cut off all private interest in the realm, the people will not be pleased.

sentences.zh: 不澄其源而欲止天下之貪，則人不悅。

translations.literal: If the source is not clarified yet one wishes to stop greed throughout all under Heaven, then the people are not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: If the source is not clarified yet one wishes to stop greed throughout the realm, the people will not be pleased.

sentences.zh: 夫必有是數者，斯足以召怨而致災。

translations.literal: When these several conditions exist, they suffice to summon resentment and bring on calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When these conditions exist, they suffice to summon resentment and bring on calamity.

sentences.zh: 願陛下捐內帑以絕壅利之謗；

translations.literal: I wish that Your Majesty would donate from the inner treasury to cut off the slander of hoarded profit;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty donate from the inner treasury to cut off the slander of hoarded profit;

sentences.zh: 出嬪嬙以節用度之奢。

translations.literal: release palace women to restrain the extravagance of expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: release palace women to restrain extravagant spending.

sentences.zh: 弄權之貂寺素為天下之所共惡者，屏之絕之；

translations.literal: eunuchs who manipulate power, long jointly hated by all under Heaven — screen them off and cut them off;
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs who manipulate power, long hated throughout the realm — remove them and cut them off;

sentences.zh: 毒民之恩澤侯嘗為百姓之所憤者，黜之棄之。

translations.literal: favor-granted marquises who harm the people and have aroused the people's anger — dismiss them and cast them off.
translations.idiomatic: favor-granted marquises who harm the people and have aroused public anger — dismiss them and cast them off.

sentences.zh: 擇忠鯁敢言之士置之臺諫，以通關鬲之壅；

translations.literal: select loyal and blunt men who dare to speak and place them in the Censorate and Remonstrance Bureau, to open the blockage of barriers and partitions;
translations.idiomatic: Select loyal and blunt men who dare to speak and place them in the Censorate and Remonstrance Bureau, to open blocked channels of communication;

sentences.zh: 選慈惠忠信之人使為守宰，以保元氣之殘。

translations.literal: choose benevolent, kind, loyal, and trustworthy men to serve as prefects and magistrates, to preserve what remains of the vital energy.
translations.idiomatic: choose benevolent, loyal, and trustworthy men to serve as prefects and magistrates, to preserve what remains of the realm's vital energy.

sentences.zh: 又必稽乾、淳以來，凡利源窠名之在百司庶府者，悉隸其舊，以濟經用之急；

translations.literal: One must also examine since the Qianchun and Chunyou reigns all profit sources and nest names in the hundred offices and various bureaus, restore them all to their former jurisdiction, to relieve the urgency of routine expenditures;
translations.idiomatic: One must also examine all profit sources and special accounts in the hundred offices since the Qianchun and Chunyou reigns, restore them to their former jurisdiction, and relieve the urgency of routine expenditures;

sentences.zh: 公田派買不均之敝，聽民自陳，隨宜通變，以安田裏之生。

translations.literal: the abuse of uneven compulsory purchase of public fields — let the people state their own cases and adapt measures as appropriate, to settle the livelihood of fields and villages.
translations.idiomatic: the abuse of uneven compulsory purchase under the public-field system — let the people state their grievances and adapt measures as appropriate, to secure the livelihood of farming communities.

sentences.zh: 則人心悅、天意解矣。

translations.literal: Then the people's hearts will be pleased and the mind of Heaven will be resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Then the people's hearts will be pleased and Heaven's mind will be appeased.

sentences.zh: 人之常情，懼心每發於災異初見之時，不能不潛移於諂諛交至之後。

translations.literal: It is the constant disposition of men that fear arises when calamities and anomalies first appear, yet it cannot but secretly shift after flattery and sycophancy arrive in succession.
translations.idiomatic: It is human nature for fear to arise when calamities first appear, yet it cannot but secretly fade after flattery and sycophancy arrive in succession.

sentences.zh: 萬一過聽左右寬譬之言，曲為它說以自解，毛舉細故以塞責，而恐懼之初心弛，則下拂人心，上違天意，國之安危或未可知。

translations.literal: If by any chance Your Majesty over-listens to comforting words from those at your side, twists other explanations to excuse yourself, nitpicks minor matters to fulfill responsibility, and the original heart of fear relaxes, then below you will go against the people's hearts, above you will violate the mind of Heaven, and whether the state is safe or in peril may be unknown.
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance Your Majesty listens too readily to comforting words from those at your side, twists other explanations to excuse yourself, nitpicks minor matters to fulfill responsibility, and the original heart of fear relaxes, then below you will go against the people's hearts, above you will violate Heaven's will, and whether the state stands safe or in peril may be unknown.

sentences.zh: 又曰：“損玉食，不若損內帑、卻貢奉之為實。

translations.literal: He also said, "To reduce jade fare is not as substantial as reducing the inner treasury and refusing tribute offerings."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Reducing imperial fare is not as substantial as reducing the inner treasury and refusing tribute offerings."

sentences.zh: 避正朝，不若塞幸門、廣忠諫之為實。

translations.literal: To avoid the regular court audience is not as substantial as blocking favor-seekers' gates and broadening loyal remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Avoiding the regular court audience is not as substantial as blocking favor-seekers' gates and broadening loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 肆大眚固所以廣仁恩，又不若擇循良、黜貪暴之為實。

translations.literal: Granting a great amnesty is indeed to extend benevolent grace, yet it is still not as substantial as selecting the law-abiding and good and dismissing the greedy and violent.
translations.idiomatic: Granting a great amnesty does extend benevolent grace, yet it is still not as substantial as selecting the law-abiding and good and dismissing the greedy and violent.

sentences.zh: 蓋天意方回而未豫，人心乍悅而旋疑，此正陰陽勝復之會，眷命隆替之機也。

translations.literal: For the mind of Heaven has just turned but is not yet at ease; the people's hearts are briefly pleased yet soon doubtful. This is precisely the juncture of yin and yang's victory and return, the moment when favor and mandate rise or fall.
translations.idiomatic: For Heaven's mind has just turned but is not yet at ease; the people's hearts are briefly pleased yet soon doubtful. This is precisely the juncture when yin and yang shift in dominance, when favor and mandate rise or fall.

sentences.zh: ”兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官，辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was concurrently Compiler of the National History Institute and Reviser of the Veritable Records Institute. He declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently Compiler of the National History Institute and Reviser of the Veritable Records Institute. He declined; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 轉對，言：“願明辯義利之限，力破系吝之私，以天自處而絕內外之分，以道制欲而黜耳目之累。

translations.literal: In rotation audience he said, "I wish that Your Majesty would clearly distinguish the boundary between righteousness and profit, vigorously break the private attachment of clinging and stinginess, take Heaven as your measure and cut off inner and outer divisions, use the Way to restrain desire and dismiss the burdens of the eyes and ears."
translations.idiomatic: In rotation audience he said, "I ask that Your Majesty clearly distinguish righteousness from profit, vigorously break attachment and stinginess, take Heaven as your measure and cut off inner and outer divisions, use the Way to restrain desire and dismiss the burdens of the senses."

sentences.zh: 毋以閨闥之賤幹公議，毋以戚畹之私紊國常。

translations.literal: Do not let the lowly of the inner quarters interfere with public discussion; do not let the private interests of imperial affines disorder the constants of state.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let the lowly of the inner quarters interfere with public discussion; do not let the private interests of imperial affines disorder the constants of state.

sentences.zh: ”乞歸田裏，不許。

translations.literal: He requested to return to his fields and village; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return to private life; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 拜太府少卿，兼職仍舊，再辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, with concurrent offices unchanged. Twice he declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, with his concurrent offices unchanged. Twice he declined; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 復上疏乞歸，不許。

translations.literal: Again he submitted a memorial requesting to return; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Again he memorialized asking to retire; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 又曰：“雷發非時，竊跡今日之事而有疑焉。

translations.literal: He also said, "Thunder issued out of season. I venture to trace today's affairs and have doubts."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Thunder issued out of season. I venture to trace today's affairs and have my doubts."

sentences.zh: 內批疊降而名器輕，宮閫不嚴而主威褻，橫恩之濫已收而復出，戢貪之詔方嚴而隨弛。

translations.literal: Inner drafts descend in layers yet titles and regalia are lightened; the inner palace is not strict yet sovereign majesty is profaned; wanton favor once gathered in is released again; the edict restraining greed is just made strict yet soon relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Inner drafts descend in layers yet titles and regalia are cheapened; the inner palace is not kept strict yet sovereign majesty is profaned; wanton favor once withdrawn is granted again; the edict restraining greed is just issued yet soon relaxed.

sentences.zh: 宮正什伍之令所以防奇邪，而或縱於乞憐之卑祠。

translations.literal: The palace regulations on groups of five and ten exist to guard against strangeness and perversity, yet sometimes indulgence is shown toward lowly shrines of begging pity.
translations.idiomatic: Palace regulations on groups of five and ten exist to guard against strangeness and perversity, yet sometimes indulgence is shown toward lowly shrines of begging pity.

sentences.zh: 緇黃出入之禁所以嚴宸居，而間惑於禬禳之小數。

translations.literal: The prohibition on black-robed and yellow-robed persons entering and leaving exists to make the imperial residence strict, yet sometimes one is misled by minor techniques of prayer and exorcism.
translations.idiomatic: The prohibition on Buddhist and Daoist clergy entering and leaving exists to keep the imperial residence strict, yet sometimes one is misled by minor techniques of prayer and exorcism.

sentences.zh: 以至彈墨未幹，而抆拭之旨已下；

translations.literal: To the point that impeachment documents are not yet dry, yet an edict wiping them clean has already been issued;
translations.idiomatic: To the point that impeachment documents are not yet dry, yet an edict wiping them clean has already been issued;

sentences.zh: 駁奏未幾，而捷出之徑已開。

translations.literal: rebuttal memorials have not long been submitted, yet a swift shortcut for approval has already been opened.
translations.idiomatic: rebuttal memorials have barely been submitted, yet a swift shortcut for approval has already been opened.

sentences.zh: 命令不疑，則陽縱而不收。

translations.literal: If commands are issued without doubt, then outwardly one indulges without reining in.
translations.idiomatic: If commands are issued without consistency, one indulges openly without reining in.

sentences.zh: 主意不堅，則陰閉而不密。

translations.literal: If the sovereign's intent is not firm, then inwardly one closes off without secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign's intent is not firm, inwardly one closes off without true resolve.

sentences.zh: 陛下可不思致災之由，而亟求所以正之哉？

translations.literal: Your Majesty — can you not reflect on the causes that bring calamity and urgently seek how to correct them?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty — can you not reflect on what brings calamity and urgently seek how to correct it?

sentences.zh: 願清其天君，以端出治之源；

translations.literal: I wish that Your Majesty would clarify the heavenly sovereign within, to rectify the source from which governance proceeds;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty clarify the heavenly sovereign within, to rectify the source from which governance proceeds;

sentences.zh: 謹其號令，以肅紀綱之本。

translations.literal: be strict in your commands and edicts, to make firm the foundation of discipline and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: be strict in your commands and edicts, to make firm the foundation of discipline and statutes.

sentences.zh: 毋牽於私恩而撓公法，毋遷於邇言而亂舊章，去讒而遠色，賤貨而貴德，則人心悅而天意得，可以開太平而兆中興也。

translations.literal: Do not be pulled by private favor and disturb public law; do not shift with nearby words and disorder old regulations; remove slander and keep distant from sensual allure; make goods low and virtue high — then the people's hearts will be pleased and the mind of Heaven obtained, and you may open great peace and presage restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Do not be pulled by private favor and disturb public law; do not shift with nearby words and disorder old regulations; remove slander and keep distant from sensual allure; make goods low and virtue high — then the people's hearts will be pleased and Heaven's will obtained, and you may open an age of great peace and presage restoration.

sentences.zh: 進權禮部侍郎兼修玉牒，再辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Acting Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently Compiler of the Imperial Genealogy. Twice he declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Acting Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently Compiler of the Imperial Genealogy. Twice he declined; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 升兼侍讀，辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was promoted to concurrent Court Reader. He declined; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to concurrent Court Reader. He declined; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 進《聖學四箴》：一曰惜日力以致其勤，二曰精體認以充其知，三曰屏嗜好以專其業，四曰謹行事以驗其用。

translations.literal: He presented the "Four Admonitions on Sagely Learning": first, cherish daily effort to achieve diligence; second, refine embodied understanding to fill one's knowledge; third, screen off indulgences to concentrate on one's work; fourth, be careful in conduct to verify one's application.
translations.idiomatic: He presented the "Four Admonitions on Sagely Learning": first, cherish daily effort to achieve diligence; second, refine embodied understanding to deepen one's knowledge; third, screen off indulgences to concentrate on one's work; fourth, be careful in conduct to verify one's application.

sentences.zh: 五乞歸田裏，帝勉留之，請益力。

translations.literal: Five times he requested to return to his fields and village. The Emperor urged him to stay, but his requests grew ever more forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Five times he asked to return to private life. The Emperor urged him to stay, but his requests grew ever more forceful.

sentences.zh: 特授集英殿修撰、知建寧府，辭，不許，乃還家。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Compiler at the Jiying Hall and Prefect of Jianning. He declined; this was not permitted, and he then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed Compiler at the Jiying Hall and prefect of Jianning. He declined; the court refused, and he returned home.

sentences.zh: 召為中書舍人，三辭，不許，請益力。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Drafting Attendant of the Central Secretariat. Three times he declined; this was not permitted, and his requests grew ever more forceful.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Drafting Attendant of the Central Secretariat. Three times he declined; the court refused, and his requests grew ever more forceful.

sentences.zh: 進顯文閣待制，依所乞予祠，辭職名，不許，遂差提舉玉隆萬壽宮。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Awaiting Draft at the Xianwen Pavilion and, according to his request, granted a shrine post. He declined the title; this was not permitted, and he was then assigned to superintend the Yulong Wanshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Awaiting Draft at the Xianwen Pavilion and, according to his request, granted a shrine post. He declined the title; the court refused, and he was assigned to superintend the Yulong Wanshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 有疾，謝醫卻藥，曰：“使我清心以順天命，毋重惱我懷。

translations.literal: When ill, he declined physicians and refused medicine, saying, "Let me clear my mind to follow Heaven's mandate; do not further trouble my heart."
translations.idiomatic: When ill, he declined physicians and refused medicine, saying, "Let me clear my mind to follow Heaven's mandate; do not further trouble my heart."

sentences.zh: ”拱手三揖乃卒。

translations.literal: He joined his hands, bowed three times, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He joined his hands, bowed three times, and died.

sentences.zh: 詔特贈四官至中奉大夫，謚文安。

translations.literal: An edict specially granted four ranks of posthumous office up to Grand Master of Palace Attendance, with the posthumous title Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially granted four ranks of posthumous office up to Grand Master of Palace Attendance, with the posthumous title Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 景緯天性孝友，雅誌沖淡，親沒無意仕進，故其立朝之日不久雲。

translations.literal: Jingwei was by nature filial and friendly, and his elegant aspiration was tranquil simplicity. When his parents died he had no wish to advance in office; therefore his days at court were not long.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwei was by nature filial and friendly, with an elegant aspiration toward tranquil simplicity. After his parents died he had no wish to advance in office; therefore his days at court were brief.

sentences.zh: 馮去非字可遷，南康都昌人。

translations.literal: Feng Qufei, courtesy name Keqian, was a native of Duchang in Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qufei, styled Keqian, came from Duchang in Nankang.

sentences.zh: 父椅字儀之，家居授徒，所註《易》、《書》、《詩》、《語》、《孟》、《太極圖》，《西銘輯說》，《孝經章句》，《喪禮小學》，《孔子弟子傳》，《讀史記》及詩文、誌錄，合二百餘卷。

translations.literal: His father Yi, courtesy name Yizhi, lived at home teaching disciples. His commentaries on the Changes, Documents, Odes, Analects, Mencius, Diagram of the Supreme Polarity, Collected Explanations of the Western Inscription, Chapter and Sentence Commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety, Elementary Learning on Mourning Rites, Biographies of Confucius's Disciples, Reading the Records of the Grand Historian, together with poetry, prose, records, and annals, totaled more than two hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi, styled Yizhi, lived at home teaching disciples. His commentaries on the Changes, Documents, Odes, Analects, Mencius, Diagram of the Supreme Polarity, Collected Explanations of the Western Inscription, chapter-and-sentence commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety, Elementary Learning on Mourning Rites, Biographies of Confucius's Disciples, Reading the Records of the Grand Historian, together with poetry, prose, records, and annals, totaled more than two hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 徐霖字景說，衢州西安人。

translations.literal: Xu Lin, courtesy name Jingshuo, was a native of Xi'an in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Lin, styled Jingshuo, came from Xi'an in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 年十三，有誌聖人之道，取所作文焚之，研精《六經》之奧，控賾先儒心傳之要。

translations.literal: At thirteen he aspired to the Way of the sages, took the compositions he had written and burned them, and delved into the profundities of the Six Classics, grasping the essentials of the heart-transmission of former Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he aspired to the Way of the sages, burned his earlier compositions, and delved into the profundities of the Six Classics, grasping the essentials of the heart-transmission of former Confucians.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，試禮部第一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunyou he ranked first in the Ministry of Rites examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1244 he ranked first in the Ministry of Rites examination.

sentences.zh: 知貢舉官入見，理宗曰：“第一名得人。

translations.literal: When the examination superintendent entered audience, Emperor Lizong said, "The first-place man is a worthy man."
translations.idiomatic: When the examination superintendent entered audience, Emperor Lizong said, "The first-place candidate is a worthy man."

sentences.zh: ”嘉獎再三。

translations.literal: He praised him again and again.
translations.idiomatic: He praised him again and again.

sentences.zh: 登第，授沅州教授。

translations.literal: When he passed the examination he was appointed Professor of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed the examination he was appointed professor in Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時宰相史嵩之挾邊功要君，植黨專國。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Councillor Shi Songzhi, relying on frontier merit to coerce the ruler, planted a faction and monopolized the state.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chief Councillor Shi Songzhi, relying on frontier merit to coerce the ruler, built a faction and monopolized the state.

sentences.zh: 霖上疏歷言其奸深之狀，以為：“其先也奪陛下之心，其次奪士大夫之心，而其甚也奪豪傑之心。

translations.literal: Lin submitted a memorial enumerating the depth of his treachery, saying, "First he seizes Your Majesty's mind; next he seizes the minds of scholar-officials; and at the extreme he seizes the minds of outstanding men."
translations.idiomatic: Lin submitted a memorial enumerating the depth of his treachery, saying, "First he seizes Your Majesty's mind; next he seizes the minds of scholar-officials; and at the extreme he seizes the minds of outstanding men."

sentences.zh: 今日之士大夫，嵩之皆變化其心而收攝之矣。

translations.literal: Today's scholar-officials — Songzhi has transformed their minds and gathered them in.
translations.idiomatic: Today's scholar-officials — Songzhi has transformed their minds and brought them under his control.

sentences.zh: 且其變化之術甚深，非章章然號於人使之為小人也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the art by which he transforms them is very deep — it is not by openly proclaiming to others and making them into petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the art by which he transforms them runs very deep — it is not by openly proclaiming to others and making them into petty men.

sentences.zh: 常於善類擇其質柔氣弱易以奪之者，親任一二，其或稍有異已，則潛棄而擯遠之，以風其餘。

translations.literal: He constantly selects from the good sort those whose substance is soft and whose spirit is weak and easy to sway, personally entrusts one or two, and if any show the slightest difference from himself, secretly abandons and banishes them far off, to influence the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly selects from the good sort those whose substance is soft and whose spirit is weak and easy to sway, personally entrusts one or two, and if any show the slightest difference from himself, secretly abandons and banishes them, to influence the rest.

sentences.zh: 彼以名節之尊不足以易富貴之願，義利之辯亦終暗於妻妾宮室之私，則亦從之而已。

translations.literal: When they find that the honor of reputation and integrity is insufficient to exchange for the desire for wealth and rank, and the debate between righteousness and profit is ultimately obscured by the private interests of wives, concubines, palaces, and chambers, then they simply follow along.
translations.idiomatic: When they find that the honor of reputation and integrity is insufficient to outweigh the desire for wealth and rank, and the debate between righteousness and profit is ultimately obscured by private interests of wives, concubines, and palaces, then they simply follow along.

sentences.zh: ”疏奏，見者吐舌，為霖危之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, those who saw it stuck out their tongues and feared for Lin's safety.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, those who saw it were astonished and feared for Lin's safety.

sentences.zh: 未幾，嵩之匿父喪求起復，君子並起而攻之，上大感悟。

translations.literal: Before long Songzhi concealed his father's mourning and sought to resume office. Gentlemen rose together to attack him, and the Emperor was greatly awakened.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Songzhi concealed his father's mourning and sought to resume office. Gentlemen rose together to attack him, and the Emperor was greatly awakened.

sentences.zh: 丞相範鐘進所召試館職二人，上思霖之忠，親去其一，易霖名。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Fan Zhong presented the two men summoned for examination for archival posts. The Emperor, mindful of Lin's loyalty, personally removed one name and replaced it with Lin's.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Fan Zhong presented the two men summoned for examination for archival posts. The Emperor, mindful of Lin's loyalty, personally removed one name and replaced it with Lin's.

sentences.zh: 及試，則曰：“人主無自強之誌，大臣有患失之心，故元良未建，兇奸未竄。

translations.literal: At the examination he said, "When the ruler lacks the will for self-strengthening and great ministers have hearts of gain and loss, therefore the heir is not established and vicious traitors are not driven off."
translations.idiomatic: At the examination he said, "When the ruler lacks the will for self-strengthening and great ministers harbor hearts of gain and loss, the heir is not established and vicious traitors are not driven off."

sentences.zh: ”是時，丞相杜範已薨，而鐘雖得位，畏奸人覆出為己禍故也。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Councillor Du Fan had already died, yet although Zhong obtained office, he feared that vicious men would reemerge and become a calamity to himself.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chief Councillor Du Fan had already died, yet although Zhong obtained office, he feared that vicious men would reemerge and become a threat to himself.

sentences.zh: 擢秘書省正字，霖辭不獲命，遂就職。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Corrector of the Secretariat. Lin declined but could not obtain permission and thereupon took up office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Corrector of the Secretariat. Lin declined but could not obtain permission and thereupon took up office.

sentences.zh: 會日食，霖應詔上封事曰：“日，陽類也，天理也，君子也。

translations.literal: When a solar eclipse occurred, by imperial order Lin submitted a sealed memorial saying, "The sun is of the yang category, the principle of Heaven, and the gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: When a solar eclipse occurred, Lin submitted a sealed memorial by imperial order, saying, "The sun belongs to the yang category; it is Heaven's principle and the gentleman."

sentences.zh: 吾心之天理不能勝乎人欲，朝廷之君子不能勝乎小人。

translations.literal: The principle of Heaven in my mind cannot overcome human desire; the gentlemen at court cannot overcome petty men.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of Heaven in one's mind cannot overcome human desire; the gentlemen at court cannot overcome petty men.

sentences.zh: 宮闈之私匿未屏，瑣闥之奸邪未辯，臺臣之討賊不決，精祲感浹，日為之食。

translations.literal: Private concealments in the palace quarters are not yet removed; treacherous evil in the inner gates is not yet distinguished; censorial officials' pursuit of traitors is not resolved — the subtle essence is moved and penetrated, and the sun is eaten.
translations.idiomatic: Private concealments in the palace quarters are not yet removed; treacherous evil in the inner gates is not yet distinguished; censorial officials' pursuit of traitors is not resolved — the subtle essence is stirred and penetrated, and the sun is devoured.

sentences.zh: ”又數言建立太子。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly spoke on establishing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly spoke on establishing the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 遷校書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Collator.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Collator.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，大旱，霖應詔言：“諫議大夫不易則不雨，京兆尹不易則不雨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, summer, there was great drought. Lin, in response to an edict, said, "If the Remonstrating Censor is not replaced, there will be no rain; if the Capital Intendant is not replaced, there will be no rain."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Chunyou (1247), during summer, a severe drought struck. Responding to an imperial edict, Xu Lin said, "Unless the Remonstrating Censor is replaced, there will be no rain; unless the Capital Intendant is replaced, there will be no rain."

sentences.zh: ”不報，去國。

translations.literal: There was no reply, and he left the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not respond, and he left the capital.

sentences.zh: 上遣著作郎姚希得留之，不還。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Compiler of the Secretariat Yao Xide to detain him; he did not return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yao Xide, compiler of the Secretariat, to persuade him to stay, but Lin would not return.

sentences.zh: 御筆改合入官，乃改宣教郎。

translations.literal: By the emperor's own brush his qualification to enter office was changed, and he was changed to Instructor Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally altered his status as one fit for office and instead appointed him Instructor Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 霖屢辭，曰：“向為身死而不敢欺其君父，今以官高而自眩於平生，失其本心，何以暴其忠誌？

translations.literal: Lin repeatedly declined, saying, "Formerly I would not deceive my ruler and father even at the cost of my body; now I dazzle myself throughout life because of high office, losing my original heart — how can I display my loyal purpose?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin declined again and again, saying, "Once I would not deceive my sovereign and father even on pain of death; now high rank blinds me to what I have always been, and I lose my true heart — how then can I show forth loyal resolve?"

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“誌貴乎潔，忠尚乎精，即有取，則自蹈於垢汙矣。

translations.literal: He also said, "Purpose values purity; loyalty esteems refinement — once one accepts appointment, one treads into filth oneself."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Ambition must stay clean, loyalty must stay keen — accept office and you walk straight into stain and disgrace."

sentences.zh: 八年夏，添差通判信州，霖皆力辭，竟未拜，改秩之命故也。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, summer, he was given added duty as vice prefect of Xin Prefecture; Lin strenuously declined all and ultimately never assumed the post, because of the order that had changed his rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Chunyou (1248), during summer, he was assigned added duty as vice prefect of Xinzhou; Lin refused forcefully each time and never took up the post, owing to the earlier order that had altered his rank.

sentences.zh: 尋令守臣勉諭之，特改宣教郎、主管雲臺觀，霖乃拜受。

translations.literal: Soon the frontier official was ordered to urge him on; he was specially made Instructor Gentleman and director of Yuntai Observatory, and Lin then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward local authorities were instructed to press him; he was specially appointed Instructor Gentleman and director of the Yuntai Observatory, and Lin at last accepted.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷秘書省著作郎，累辭，不許。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Compiler in the Secretariat; he declined repeatedly and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Chunyou (1252) he was promoted to compiler in the Secretariat; he declined again and again, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 兼國史編修、實錄檢討，上曰：“今日所當言者，當備陳之。

translations.literal: He also served as compiler of the National History and reviser of the Veritable Records. The Emperor said, "What ought to be said today should be fully set forth."
translations.idiomatic: He also served as compiler of the National History and reviser of the Veritable Records. The emperor told him, "Say fully whatever ought to be said today."

sentences.zh: ”霖復以正太子名為言，又奏：“萬化之本在心，存心之法在敬。

translations.literal: Lin again spoke on establishing the crown prince's name, and memorialized, "The root of all transformation is in the heart; the method of preserving the heart is reverence."
translations.idiomatic: Lin again urged that the crown prince's name be properly established, and memorialized, "The root of ten thousand transformations lies in the heart; the way to preserve the heart lies in reverence."

sentences.zh: ”兼權尚左郎官，兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently as acting director of the Left Department and as lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He also held concurrent appointments as acting director of the Left Department and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 乃上疏言：“葉大有陰柔奸黠，為群憸冠，不宜久長臺諫，乞斥去。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying, "Ye Dayou is covertly soft, treacherous and cunning, the head of a host of villains — unsuitable to hold censorial remonstrance posts for long; I beg that he be expelled."
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized, "Ye Dayou is smooth on the surface yet treacherous and slick, chief among the deceivers — he should not long hold a remonstrance post on the Censorate; I beg that he be removed."

sentences.zh: ”不報。

translations.literal: There was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 兼權左司。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently as acting chief of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He also concurrently acted as chief of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 霖知無不言，於是讒嫉者思以中傷，而上亦不悅。

translations.literal: Lin spoke without withholding anything; thereupon slanderers and jealous men sought to strike him at the center, and the Emperor was also displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Lin withheld nothing in his remonstrance; jealous slanderers then plotted to ruin him, and the emperor too grew displeased.

sentences.zh: 乞補外，知撫州。

translations.literal: He requested an outside appointment and was made prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to serve outside the capital and was appointed prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 祠先賢，寬租賦，振饑窮，誅悍將，建營砦，幾一月而政舉化行。

translations.literal: He sacrificed to former worthies, eased rent and tax burdens, relieved the hungry and destitute, executed brutal generals, and built camps and stockades; within nearly a month government was in order and transformation spread.
translations.idiomatic: He offered sacrifices to sage predecessors, lightened rents and taxes, succored the starving and poor, executed violent commanders, and built stockaded camps — within about a month his administration was sound and reform took hold.

sentences.zh: 以言去，士民遮道，不得行，及暝，始由徑以出。

translations.literal: He was removed because of his words; gentry and commoners blocked the road so he could not pass; at dusk he went out by a bypath.
