translations.idiomatic: Dismissed for his outspokenness, scholars and townspeople blocked the roads so he could not leave; only at nightfall did he slip out by a hidden path.

sentences.zh: 寶祐元年，差知衡州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoyou he was assigned as prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoyou (1253) he was assigned prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，當之官，遂辭，差知袁州。

translations.literal: In the third year, when he was to take office, he declined; he was then assigned as prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1255), when the time came to take up his post, he declined; he was then reassigned prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，丁外艱，哀毀號絕，水漿不入口七日。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered mourning for his father's death; grief and devastation stopped his voice; for seven days he took neither water nor gruel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1257) he mourned his father's death; grief shattered him until his cries ceased, and for seven days he refused water and broth.

sentences.zh: 明年開慶元年，差主管崇禧觀。

translations.literal: The next year, the first year of Kaiqing, he was assigned director of the Chongxi Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the first year of Kaiqing (1259), he was assigned director of the Chongxi Observatory.

sentences.zh: 景定二年，知汀州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingding he was made prefect of Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingding (1261) he became prefect of Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The year after, he died.

sentences.zh: 將終，語其長子心亨曰：“有生必有死，自古聖賢皆然，吾復何憾。

translations.literal: As death approached he told his eldest son Sinheng, "Where there is life there must be death; sages and worthies have been thus since antiquity — what further regret have I?"
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his eldest son Sinheng, "Life must end in death; sages and worthies have always known this — what regret can I still have?"

sentences.zh: ”尚書省請加優異，詔與一子恩澤。

translations.literal: The Secretariat requested added honors; an edict granted one son a boon of office.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat requested exceptional honors; an edict granted a preferment to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 度宗賜祭田百畝，以旌直臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Duzong granted one hundred mu of sacrificial fields to commend the upright minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Duzong granted a hundred mu of sacrificial fields in recognition of his integrity.

sentences.zh: 霖間居衢，守遊鈞築精舍，聘霖為學者講道，是日聽者三千餘人。

translations.literal: When Lin lived at leisure in Quzhou, Prefect You Jun built a refined hall, engaged Lin to expound the Way for scholars, and on that day listeners numbered more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: While Lin lived in retirement at Quzhou, the prefect You Jun built a lecture hall and invited him to teach; more than three thousand people heard him speak that day.

sentences.zh: 徐宗仁字求心，信之永豐人。

translations.literal: Xu Zongren, courtesy name Qiuxin, was a native of Yongfeng in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zongren, style name Qiuxin, was a native of Yongfeng in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳祐十年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the tenth year of Chunyou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Chunyou (1250).

sentences.zh: 歷官為國子監主簿。

translations.literal: He served in office as recorder of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as recorder of the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 開慶元年，伏闕上書曰：

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiqing he prostrated himself at the palace gate and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiqing (1259) he kowtowed at the palace gate and submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 賞罰者，軍國之綱紀。

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments are the discipline of army and state.
translations.idiomatic: Reward and punishment are the discipline of army and state.

sentences.zh: 賞罰不明，則綱紀不立。

translations.literal: When rewards and punishments are not clear, discipline is not established.
translations.idiomatic: When reward and punishment are unclear, that discipline collapses.

sentences.zh: 今天下如器之欹而未墜於地，存亡之機，固不容發。

translations.literal: Today the realm is like a vessel tilting but not yet fallen to earth; the hinge of survival and ruin brooks no delay.
translations.idiomatic: Today the empire is like a vessel tilting but not yet fallen; the moment that decides survival or ruin allows no delay.

sentences.zh: 兵虛將惰，而力匱財殫，環視四境，類不足恃；

translations.literal: Troops are hollow and generals slack, while strength is exhausted and wealth depleted; looking about the four borders, nothing seems fit to rely on;
translations.idiomatic: The armies are hollow and the generals indolent, strength spent and treasury drained; look around the frontiers and little seems dependable;

sentences.zh: 而所恃以維持人心、奔走豪傑者，惟陛下賞罰之微權在耳。

translations.literal: Yet what maintains men's hearts and drives heroes to strive is only Your Majesty's subtle power of reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what still holds hearts together and moves heroes to serve is nothing but Your Majesty's subtle power of reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 權在陛下，而陛下不知所以用之，則未墜者安保其終不墜乎？

translations.literal: That power lies with Your Majesty, yet Your Majesty does not know how to use it — can what has not fallen be assured never to fall in the end?
translations.idiomatic: That power rests in Your Majesty's hands, yet Your Majesty does not know how to wield it — can a realm not yet fallen be sure it will never fall?

sentences.zh: 臣為此懼久矣。

translations.literal: Your servant has long feared this.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has long lived in dread of this.

sentences.zh: 陛下當危急之時，出金幣賜土田，授節鉞，分爵秩，尺寸之功，在所必賞。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty faced peril, you dispensed gold and coins, granted fields, conferred tally-seals, divided ranks — the smallest merit was inevitably rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: In time of crisis Your Majesty showered gold, granted land, bestowed command seals, and handed out ranks — the least merit was sure to be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 故當悉心效力，圖報萬分可也。

translations.literal: Therefore they ought to give their utmost and repay you ten-thousandfold — that would be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Men should have thrown themselves into service and repaid you a thousandfold — that was only right.

sentences.zh: 而自幹腹之兵越江逾廣以來，凡閱數月，尚未聞有死戰陣、死封疆、死城郭者，豈賞罰不足以勸懲之耶？

translations.literal: Yet since the crack troops crossed the Yangtze and passed Guangdong, several months have passed and we have not yet heard of men dying in battle, dying for the frontier, or dying for the walls — is it that reward and punishment cannot encourage and restrain?
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the elite armies crossed the Yangtze and pressed into Guangdong, months have passed without word of men dying in battle, on the borders, or for the cities — are rewards and punishments no longer fit to move men?

sentences.zh: 今通國之所謂佚罰者，不過丁大全、袁玠、沈翥、張鎮、吳衍、翁應弼、石正則、王立愛、高鑄之徒，而首惡則董宋臣也。

translations.literal: Now what the whole realm calls unpunished evildoers are no more than Ding Daquan, Yuan Jie, Shen Zhu, Zhang Zhen, Wu Yan, Weng Yingbi, Shi Zhengze, Wang Liai, Gao Zhu, and the like — while the chief culprit is Dong Songchen.
translations.idiomatic: Today those the realm calls unpunished are no more than Ding Daquan, Yuan Jie, Shen Zhu, Zhang Zhen, Wu Yan, Weng Yingbi, Shi Zhengze, Wang Liai, Gao Zhu, and men like them — while the ringleader is Dong Songchen.

sentences.zh: 是以廷紳抗疏，學校叩閽，至有欲借尚方劍為陛下除惡。

translations.literal: Therefore court gentlemen submitted confronting memorials and schools beat on the gate, even to the point of wishing to borrow the emperor's execution sword to remove evil for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials have flooded in with indicting memorials; students have battered the gates, some even begging to borrow the imperial sword to purge evil for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 而陛下乃釋而不問，豈真欲愛護此數人而重咈千萬人之心？

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty released them and did not inquire — do you truly wish to protect these few men and heavily offend the hearts of millions?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty let them go unscathed — do you truly mean to shield these few and deeply affront the hearts of millions?

sentences.zh: 天下之事勢急矣，朝廷之紀綱壞矣。

translations.literal: The situation of the realm is urgent; the discipline of the court is ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The realm's peril is acute; the court's discipline is broken.

sentences.zh: 若誤國之罪不誅，則用兵之士不勇。

translations.literal: If crimes that ruined the state are not punished, then men who go to war will not be brave.
translations.idiomatic: If those who wrecked the state are not punished, soldiers will not fight bravely.

sentences.zh: 今東南一隅天下，已半壞於此數人之手，而罰不損其豪毛。

translations.literal: Now half the realm in the southeast has already been ruined in these men's hands, yet punishment has not touched a hair on them.
translations.idiomatic: Half the empire in the southeast has already been ruined by these men, yet not a hair on their heads has been harmed.

sentences.zh: 彼方擁厚貲，挾聲色，高臥華屋，而使陛下與二三大臣焦心勞思，可乎？

translations.literal: They hug their great wealth, carry off pleasure and song, lounge in splendid houses, while Your Majesty and two or three great ministers fret and labor — can this be right?
translations.idiomatic: They clutch vast fortunes, indulge in pleasure, and sleep in grand houses while Your Majesty and a few great ministers burn with anxiety — can this stand?

sentences.zh: 三軍之在行者，豈不憤然不平曰：“稔禍者誰歟，而使我捐軀兵革之間？

translations.literal: Will not the troops on campaign cry out in rage, "Who piled up disaster, that we should spill our lives between arms and armor?"
translations.idiomatic: Will not soldiers in the field cry in fury, "Who brought on this ruin, that we must die between sword and spear?"

sentences.zh: ”百姓之罹難者，豈不群然胥怨曰：“召亂者誰歟，而使我流血鋒鏑之下？

translations.literal: Will not the people who suffer calamity complain together, "Who summoned chaos, that we must bleed under spear and blade?"
translations.idiomatic: Will not suffering commoners wail together, "Who stirred up chaos, that we must bleed beneath the blades?"

sentences.zh: ”陛下亦嘗一念及此乎？

translations.literal: Has Your Majesty ever once reflected on this?
translations.idiomatic: Has Your Majesty ever paused to think of this?

sentences.zh: 又極論邊事，謂惠褻而威不振。

translations.literal: He also argued to the utmost on frontier affairs, saying that kindness had grown excessive while awe was not raised.
translations.idiomatic: He also pressed frontier policy to the limit, arguing that excessive indulgence had sapped imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 論董宋臣盤固日久，蒙蔽日久。

translations.literal: He argued that Dong Songchen had entrenched himself for a long time and had long deceived the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He charged that Dong Songchen had entrenched his power for years and had long blinded the court.

sentences.zh: 又請“使有言責者皆得以盡其言，則國論伸而國威振，臣雖屏處山林，亦有生氣”。

translations.literal: He also requested that "those holding the duty to speak should all be able to speak their fill; then national discourse will extend and national prestige rise — though your servant dwells hidden in mountains and forests, he too will breathe with life."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that "everyone charged to speak out be allowed to speak fully; then public debate will widen and national prestige revive — and though I live hidden among hills and woods, I too will feel life return."

sentences.zh: 遷國子監丞、秘書省著作佐郎，主管崇禧觀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Directorate of Education, assistant compiler in the Secretariat, and director of the Chongxi Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Imperial College, assistant compiler in the Secretariat, and director of the Chongxi Observatory.

sentences.zh: 遷考功郎官兼崇政殿說書，進讀《敬天圖》。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Evaluations, also lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall; he lectured on presenting the "Chart of Revering Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He became director of the Bureau of Evaluations and lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, where he lectured on the "Chart of Revering Heaven."

sentences.zh: 遷太府少卿兼侍講、兼侍立修註官，遷太常少卿兼國史編修、實錄檢討。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Imperial Treasury, also Court Lecturer and Attending Revision Officer; then Vice Minister of Rites, also compiler of the National History and reviser of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the Imperial Treasury, also court lecturer and attendant revision officer; then vice minister of rites, also compiler of the National History and reviser of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 知寧國府。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Ningguo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 監察御史郭閶論罷。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Guo Chang impeached and removed him.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Guo Chang memorialized for his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 危昭德，邵武人。

translations.literal: Wei Zhaode was a native of Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaode came from Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 寶祐元年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the first year of Baoyou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Baoyou (1253).

sentences.zh: 歷官為史館檢閱校勘、武學諭、宗正寺簿兼崇政殿說書，遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: He served as revising collator in the Historiography Institute, instructor at the Military School, and registrar of the Imperial Clan Court, also lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall; he was transferred to Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as historiographic collator, instructor at the Military School, and registrar of the Imperial Clan Court, also lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, before promotion to secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 疏言：“國之命在民，民之命在士大夫。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said, "The state's life lies in the people; the people's life lies in the scholar-officials."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote, "A state's lifeblood is its people; the people's lifeblood is its scholar-officials."

sentences.zh: 士大夫不廉，朘民膏血，為己甘腴，民不堪命矣。

translations.literal: When scholar-officials are not clean, they drain the people's fat and blood for their own sweet affluence, and the people cannot bear their fate."
translations.idiomatic: When officials grow corrupt, they bleed the people dry to fatten themselves, until the people can no longer endure it."

sentences.zh: ”又言：“願陛下與二三大臣察利害之實，究安危之本，明詔郡國，申嚴號令，俾急其所急，凡荒政之當舉者，不可一日而置念；

translations.literal: He also said, "I wish Your Majesty with two or three great ministers to examine the realities of benefit and harm, trace the roots of safety and danger, issue clear edicts to the prefectures, and strictly enforce commands, hastening what must be hastened — all famine governance that ought to be undertaken must not be set aside for a single day;"
translations.idiomatic: He also urged, "I beg Your Majesty and your chief ministers to weigh real gains and losses, grasp the roots of safety and peril, issue clear orders to every circuit, and enforce them strictly — press every urgent need; nothing required for famine relief may be neglected even for a day;"

sentences.zh: 緩其可緩，凡苛賦之肆擾者，易為此時之寬征。

translations.literal: Slowing what may be slowed — all harsh levies that roam and harass should in this season become lenient collection."
translations.idiomatic: Ease what can be eased — every oppressive tax that harasses the people should, in this hour, give way to lighter collection."

sentences.zh: 固結人心，乃所以延天命也。

translations.literal: To solidify men's hearts is how to extend Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Solidify popular loyalty, and you prolong Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: ”又言：“願陛下舉考課之事，內以責諸彈糾之職，外以責諸監司、郡守之計。

translations.literal: He also said, "I wish Your Majesty to undertake performance evaluations — inwardly charge the censorial duty of impeachment, outwardly charge the intendants' and prefects' plans."
translations.idiomatic: He further asked the emperor to institute performance reviews — holding censors accountable within, intendants and prefects without.

sentences.zh: 貪濁昏庸，固在必懲。

translations.literal: The greedy, corrupt, benighted, and incompetent must surely be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The greedy, corrupt, dull, and inept must surely be punished.

sentences.zh: 廉能正直，尤當示勸。

translations.literal: The clean, capable, upright, and straight must especially be shown encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The honest, capable, and upright must especially be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 察之精則黜陟之鹹服，行之力則觀聽之具孚，而課吏之實得矣。

translations.literal: When examination is refined, promotions and demotions all submit; when execution is forceful, observers are all convinced — then the reality of assessing officials is attained."
translations.idiomatic: Examine with rigor and appointment and dismissal will command belief; act with force and the court and country will trust you — then true official accountability is achieved."

sentences.zh: 進兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was promoted also to Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 又言：“民者，邦之命脈，欲壽國脈，必厚民生，欲厚民生，必寬民力。

translations.literal: He also said, "The people are the life-pulse of the state; to prolong the state's pulse one must enrich people's lives; to enrich people's lives one must ease their burdens."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued, "The people are the state's lifeblood; to keep the state alive you must enrich the people; to enrich the people you must lighten their burdens."

sentences.zh: ”且條上厲民四敝。

translations.literal: He also listed and submitted the four harms that afflict the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a detailed list of the four abuses that grind the people down.

sentences.zh: 又言：“願陛下為萬世根本之慮，為一時倉卒之防，必求安節之亨，毋招不節之咎，節之又節，則宮闈之費差省，帑藏之積自充，上用足而下不匱矣。

translations.literal: He also said, "I wish Your Majesty to plan for the state's root foundation across ten thousand generations and guard against sudden emergency in the present moment; you must seek the prosperity of measured restraint and not invite the blame of immoderation — restrain again and again, then palace expenses will be somewhat reduced and treasury stores will naturally fill — above will have sufficiency and below will not be exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to think in terms of generations, not emergencies alone — to practice frugality until it prospers and never court the guilt of waste; cut again and again, and palace costs shrink while the treasury fills — the court will have enough and the people will not be drained.

sentences.zh: ”又乞“察欣瘁休戚之故，酌利害損益之宜，孰為當因，孰為當革，孰為可罷，孰為可行，則折衷泉貨而遠近便，開通關梁而商賈行。

translations.literal: He also requested, "Examine the causes of joy, weariness, rest, and sorrow; weigh benefit and harm, loss and gain — what ought to be retained, what ought to be reformed, what can be abolished, what can be carried out — then balance currency and the near and far will be convenient; open pass and bridge and merchants and traders will travel."
translations.idiomatic: He also begged the court to study what pleases and what wearies the people, judge what helps or harms them, decide what to keep or change, what to abolish or enact — harmonize currency so all regions benefit, open passes and bridges so trade may flow.

sentences.zh: 下修身奉法之詔，而吏得自新；

translations.literal: Issue an edict for self-cultivation and obedience to law, and officials may renew themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim self-restraint and lawful rule so officials may reform themselves;

sentences.zh: 出輸倉助貸之令，而民免貴糴；

translations.literal: Issue orders to ship grain from storehouses and grant loans, and the people will escape dear purchase of grain;
translations.idiomatic: Order granaries to lend grain so the people escape ruinous prices;

sentences.zh: 窒墨敕之門，而無官府黜陟之異；

translations.literal: Stop the door of ink edicts, and there will be no irregularity in government appointments and dismissals;
translations.idiomatic: Close the gate to secret edicts so civil appointments are no longer twisted;

sentences.zh: 止輪臺之議，而無疆界彼此之分，則氣脈蘇醒、意向翕合矣”。

translations.literal: Halt the debate over Luntai, and there will be no division of borders between ourselves and others — then the life-pulse will revive and intentions will unite."
translations.idiomatic: End expansion debates like the Luntain dispute so frontiers are not torn between us and them — then the nation's pulse will revive and all hearts will draw together."

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人兼國史編修、實錄檢討，尋遷殿中侍御史、侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Diarist, also compiler of the National History and reviser of the Veritable Records; soon he was transferred to Palace Censor and Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to diarist, also compiler of the National History and reviser of the Veritable Records; soon he became palace censor and attending censor.

sentences.zh: 諫作宗陽宮。

translations.literal: He remonstrated against building the Zongyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated against construction of the Zongyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 權工部侍郎兼同修國史實錄院，乞致仕，特轉一官。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Works, also co-compiler at the National History and Veritable Records Institute; he requested retirement and was specially promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: As acting vice minister of works and co-compiler of the national history and veritable records, he asked to retire and was specially promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 昭德在經筵，以《易》、《春秋》、《大學衍義》進講，反覆規正者甚多。

translations.literal: Zhaode at the Classics Mat advanced lectures on the "Changes," the "Spring and Autumn," and the "Extended Meaning of the Great Learning"; repeatedly admonishing and correcting, he did so in many matters.
translations.idiomatic: At the classics mat Zhaode lectured on the "Changes," the "Spring and Autumn," and the "Extended Meaning of the Great Learning," admonishing and correcting the emperor again and again on many points.

sentences.zh: 所著《春山文集》。

translations.literal: He authored the "Collected Works of Spring Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Collected Works of Spring Mountain.

sentences.zh: 子徹孫，鹹淳元年進士。

translations.literal: His son Zhesun passed the jinshi in the first year of Xianchun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhesun passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Xianchun (1265).

sentences.zh: 陳塏字子爽，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Chen Kai, courtesy name Zishuang, was a native of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kai, style name Zishuang, was a native of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 歷京湖制置使司主管機宜文字，差知德安府，加直寶謨閣、江西提點刑獄，改直敷文閣、提舉千秋鴻禧觀，轉司農寺丞、主管崇道觀、知安慶府。

translations.literal: He served as drafting officer on the staff of the Jing-Hu Pacification Commission, was assigned prefect of De'an Prefecture, was made Honorary Master of the Hall of Precious Instruction and Jiangxi Intendant of Judicial Affairs, changed to Honorary Master of the Hall of Dispersing Culture and director of the Qianqiu Hongxi Observatory, then transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, director of the Chongdao Observatory, and prefect of Anqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as drafting officer on the Jing-Hu pacification staff, was posted prefect of De'an, advanced to honorary master of the Hall of Precious Instruction and Jiangxi judicial intendant, then to honorary master of the Hall of Dispersing Culture and director of the Qianqiu Hongxi Observatory, and finally to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, director of the Chongdao Observatory, and prefect of Anqing.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，加直顯謨閣、湖南提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Summoned to court; made Honorary Master of the Hall of Manifest Instruction and Hunan Intendant of Judicial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was made honorary master of the Hall of Manifest Instruction and Hunan judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 再召為右司郎官，加直寶文閣知隆興府、江西安撫使，改知江州，主管江西安撫司事。

translations.literal: Again summoned as Right Secretariat director; made Honorary Master of the Palace of Literary Glory and prefect of Longxing, Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner; changed to prefect of Jiang Prefecture and chief of the Jiangxi Pacification Office.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned again as director of the Right Secretariat, he became honorary master of the Palace of Literary Glory, prefect of Longxing, and Jiangxi pacification commissioner; he was then reassigned prefect of Jiangzhou with charge of Jiangxi pacification affairs.

sentences.zh: 召為右司郎官，進直龍圖閣、浙西提點刑獄，遷司農少卿，以秘閣修撰知慶元府兼沿海制置副使，遷大理卿，進右文殿修撰、知平江府兼淮、浙發運使。

translations.literal: Summoned as Right Secretariat director; promoted Honorary Master of the Dragon Diagram and Zhexi Judicial Intendant; transferred Vice Minister of Revenue; made Secretariat Compiler and prefect of Qingyuan with concurrent Coastal Pacification Vice Commissioner; transferred Grand Court Administrator; advanced Right Palace of Literary Cultivation Compiler, prefect of Pingjiang, and Huai-Zhe Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as director of the Right Secretariat, he rose to honorary master of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Zhexi judicial intendant, then vice minister of revenue; as secretariat compiler he governed Qingyuan while serving as coastal pacification vice commissioner; he then became grand court administrator, advanced to right palace compiler of literary cultivation, prefect of Pingjiang, and Huai-Zhe transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎趙必願舉塏最，詔特轉一官，遷太府卿、司農卿，權工部侍郎兼同詳定敕令官，兼中書門下省檢正諸房公事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Biyuan praised Kai as foremost; an edict specially promoted him one rank; he was transferred Grand Court Administrator and Vice Minister of Revenue, acting Vice Minister of Works, also co-reviser of Statutes and concurrently Rectifier of the Bureau of State Affairs in the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Biyuan, vice minister of revenue, ranked Kai first in merit; an edict specially promoted him one rank; he was made grand court administrator and vice minister of revenue, then acting vice minister of works, also co-reviser of statutes and concurrently rectifier of affairs in the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 入奏，言：“願陛下轉移世道之樞機，砥礪士大夫之廉恥，使知名義為重，利祿為輕。

translations.literal: Entering to memorialize, he said, "I wish Your Majesty to shift the pivot of the world's way and sharpen the integrity and shame of scholar-officials, making fame and duty heavy and profit and salary light."
translations.idiomatic: Appearing before the throne, he said, "I beg Your Majesty to turn the world's moral hinge and renew officials' sense of honor, so that principle weighs more than emolument."

sentences.zh: 久去國以恬退聞者召之，久立朝以更叠請者從之，甘言容悅者必斥，真情丐閑者勿留。

translations.literal: Those long away from office and known for tranquil withdrawal — summon them; those long at court and repeatedly requesting transfer — let them go; sweet words and pleasing faces — surely expel; honest words and true requests for leisure — do not detain."
translations.idiomatic: Recall those who have long left office and are known for quiet integrity; release those who linger at court only to jockey for new posts; drive out flatterers; do not keep back officials who honestly seek retirement."

sentences.zh: 如此，則君臣上下皆以真實相與，四維既張，士大夫難進易退之風，當見於聖世，人才幸甚！

translations.literal: If it is thus, ruler and ministers above and below will all deal with each other in truth; the four bonds once stretched, the custom of scholar-officials being hard to advance and easy to withdraw will appear in a sage age — how fortunate for talent!
translations.idiomatic: Then sovereign and ministers will treat one another sincerely; with the four bonds taut, the old ideal of officials hard to entice and easy to dismiss will flourish in a sage reign — a blessing for men of talent!

sentences.zh: ”又言：“請以從官仿古昔人從出藩之意，其從臣為諸路憲漕，則以提點刑獄使、轉運使系銜，假之‘使’名，示與庶官別，仍乞除授自臣始。

translations.literal: He also said, "I request that attendant officials follow the ancient meaning of followers going out to the provinces; when such followers serve as circuit intendants and transport commissioners, let their titles be Intendant of Judicial Affairs or Transport Commissioner, lend them the title 'commissioner' to show distinction from ordinary officials — and I beg that such appointments begin with me."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I ask that follow-officers be sent to the provinces in the ancient spirit of an entourage abroad; where such men serve as judicial or transport officials, let them bear those titles with the added designation 'commissioner' to mark them above common posts — and I beg that appointments on this model begin with myself."

sentences.zh: ”自是屢言於帝前，不許。

translations.literal: "From then on he repeatedly spoke of this before the emperor; it was not permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he pressed the proposal again and again at court, but the throne would not assent.

sentences.zh: 以言罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed because of his remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He lost office for having spoken out.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進集英殿修撰、知婺州，改知太平州兼江東轉運副使。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted Compiler in the Hall for Cultivation of Literature and made prefect of Wu; he was reassigned prefect of Taiping while serving concurrently as vice transport commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he rose to compiler in the Hall for Cultivation of Literature and governor of Wu, then was transferred to Taiping with a concurrent post as Jiangdong vice transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 請蠲放諸郡災傷。

translations.literal: He requested remission and relief for disaster losses in the various commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to cancel levies on calamity-stricken districts throughout the circuits.

sentences.zh: 加戶部侍郎、淮東總領，尋提領江、淮茶鹽所兼知太平州。

translations.literal: He was given the additional titles of Vice Minister of Revenue and General Controller of Huaidong; soon he took charge of the Jiang-Huai Tea and Salt Agency while continuing as prefect of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted vice minister of revenue and Huaidong chief commissary, he soon headed the Jiang-Huai tea-and-salt monopoly while retaining the Taiping prefecture.

sentences.zh: 發公帑代三縣輸折絲帛錢五十萬九千三百六十餘貫。

translations.literal: He disbursed public funds to pay, on behalf of three counties, more than 509,360 strings in commuted silk-cloth money.
translations.idiomatic: From the public treasury he advanced over 509,360 strings of commuted silk tribute owed by three counties.

sentences.zh: 又作浮淮書堂以處兩淮之民而教之。

translations.literal: He also built the Floating-Huai Book Hall to house the people of the two Huai regions and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Floating-Huai Academy to settle and educate refugees from both banks of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 進顯謨閣待制、知廣州，權兵部尚書，又進寶章閣直學士、知婺州，遷權戶部尚書，尋為真，時暫兼吏部尚書，以寶文閣學士知潭州兼湖南安撫使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Master of the Hall of Manifest Instruction and made prefect of Guangzhou, acting Minister of War; again advanced to Direct Academician of the Hall of Precious Insignia and prefect of Wu; transferred to acting Minister of Revenue, soon made substantive, and for a time concurrently acting Minister of Personnel; then made Academician of the Palace of Literary Glory, prefect of Tanzhou, and Hunan Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted master of the Hall of Manifest Instruction and prefect of Guangzhou with acting charge of the Ministry of War, he was soon direct academician of the Hall of Precious Insignia at Wu, then acting and finally substantive minister of revenue, briefly acting minister of personnel as well, and finally academician of the Palace of Literary Glory governing Tanzhou as Hunan pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，以舊職提舉太平興國宮，加龍圖閣學士，依舊宮觀。

translations.literal: Summoned to court, he was appointed with his former rank to direct the Taiping Xingguo Palace, was given the Dragon Diagram Academician title, and continued in the same palace post.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was posted to direct the Taiping Xingguo Palace with his old rank, advanced to dragon-diagram academician, and left in charge of the same observatory.

sentences.zh: 久之，加端明殿學士。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was made Academician of the Hall of Sagacious Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was elevated to academician of the Hall of Sagacious Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳四年，卒，謚清毅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianchun he died; his posthumous title was Clear and Resolute.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Xianchun (1268) and was given the posthumous name Qingyi, "Clear and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 塏屢歷麾節，軍民愛戴，幕客盛多，而塏又樂薦士。

translations.literal: Kai repeatedly held military and civil commissions; soldiers and civilians loved him, his staff was large, and he delighted in recommending scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kai served many times as a regional commander; troops and people adored him, his secretariat teemed with clients, and he took pleasure in advancing men of talent.

sentences.zh: 所著《可齋瓿稿》二十卷。

translations.literal: His collected works, Kezhai Bougao, in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left Kezhai Bougao ("Drafts from the Satisfied Studio") in twenty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 楊文仲字時發，眉州彭山人。

translations.literal: Yang Wenzhong, courtesy name Shifa, was a native of Pengshan in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wenzhong, style name Shifa, came from Pengshan in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 七歲而孤。

translations.literal: He lost his father at the age of seven.
translations.idiomatic: His father died when he was seven.

sentences.zh: 母胡，年二十有八，守節自誓，教養諸子。

translations.literal: His mother Hu, aged twenty-eight, vowed to remain chaste and devoted herself to raising her sons.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Hu, only twenty-eight, swore widowhood and single-handedly reared her boys.

sentences.zh: 文仲既冠，以《春秋》貢，其母喜曰：“汝家至汝，三世以是經收效矣。

translations.literal: When Wenzhong reached manhood he presented the Spring and Autumn Annals as tribute; his mother rejoiced and said, "In your family, down to you, three generations have won success through this classic."
translations.idiomatic: Once capped, Wenzhong entered the Spring and Autumn Annals for the tribute examination; his mother exulted: "To your generation our house owes three generations of reward from this text."

sentences.zh: 淳祐七年，文仲以胄試第一入太學。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chunyou, Wenzhong ranked first in the cadet examination and entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1247 he topped the imperial-cadet trial and entered the National University.

sentences.zh: 九年，又以公試第一升內舍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again ranked first in the public examination and was promoted to the Inner Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he again led the public examination and rose to the inner lodge.

sentences.zh: 時言路頗壅，因季冬雷震，首帥同舍叩閽極言時事，有曰：“天本不怒，人激之使怒。

translations.literal: At the time the remonstrance path was largely blocked; because of winter thunder in the twelfth month he took the lead among his classmates in knocking at the palace gate and speaking bluntly on current affairs, saying among other things: "Heaven is not angry by nature; men provoke it to anger."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance was largely choked off; when winter thunder shook the twelfth month he led his classmates to the palace gate with a fierce memorial on the times, declaring: "Heaven is not angry of itself—men stir it to wrath."

sentences.zh: 人本無言，雷激之使言。

translations.literal: "Men are naturally without words; thunder stirs them to speak."
translations.idiomatic: "Men would keep silence; thunder forces them to speak."

sentences.zh: ”一時爭傳誦之。

translations.literal: For a time everyone competed to copy and recite his words.
translations.idiomatic: His lines raced through the academy, copied and chanted everywhere.

sentences.zh: 升上舍，為西廊學錄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to the Upper Lodge and made recorder of the West Corridor.
translations.idiomatic: Advanced to the upper lodge, he became recorder of the west corridor.

sentences.zh: 丞相謝方叔嘗問文仲曰：“今日何事最急？

translations.literal: The chancellor Xie Fangshu once asked Wenzhong, "What is most urgent today?"
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Xie Fangshu once asked him: "What matter is most pressing now?"

sentences.zh: ”對曰：“國本未建，莫大於此。

translations.literal: He replied, "The imperial heir is not established; nothing is greater than this."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "The succession is unsettled—nothing outweighs that."

sentences.zh: 上意未喻，當以死請可也。

translations.literal: "If the sovereign's mind is not persuaded, one should be ready to die in petitioning—that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: "If His Majesty still does not understand, one must be willing to die pleading—that alone will do."

sentences.zh: ”寶祐元年，登進士第。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoyou he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi degree in 1253.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，釋服，屬從叔父棟守婺州罷歸，寓余杭，文仲往問伊、洛之學。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother; when the mourning ended his cousin-uncle Dong, who had governed Wu Prefecture and been dismissed, was staying in Yuhang; Wenzhong went to study the learning of the Cheng brothers and Zhou Dunyi.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning he visited his cousin-uncle Dong—dismissed after governing Wu—lodging in Yuhang, and pursued the moral philosophy of the Cheng brothers and Zhou Dunyi.

sentences.zh: 調復州學教授。

translations.literal: He was assigned professor at the Fu Prefecture school.
translations.idiomatic: Posted professor at the Fu Prefecture academy.

sentences.zh: 轉運使印應飛辟入幕。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Yin Yingfei recruited him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner Yin Yingfei brought him onto his secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明嫠婦冤獄，應飛悉從文仲議，且薦之。

translations.literal: He clarified a wrongful case involving a widowed woman; Yingfei followed Wenzhong's judgment entirely and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed a miscarriage of justice against a widow; Yingfei adopted his view in full and commended him.

sentences.zh: 荊湖宣撫使趙葵署文仲佐分司幕。

translations.literal: Jing-Hu Pacification Commissioner Zhao Kui appointed Wenzhong assistant in the branch staff office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kui, pacification commissioner of Jing-Hu, named him aide on the branch staff.

sentences.zh: 姚希得、江萬里合薦文仲學為有用。

translations.literal: Yao Xide and Jiang Wanli jointly recommended Wenzhong, saying his learning was of practical use.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xide and Jiang Wanli together praised his scholarship as fit for service.

sentences.zh: 辟四川宣撫司準備差遣，添差沿海制置司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: He was recruited as preparatory dispatch officer on the Sichuan Pacification staff and given an additional assignment as clerk on the Coastal Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Sichuan pacification staff as a preparatory dispatch officer and received an additional post on the coastal pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部架閣，遷太學正，升博士。

translations.literal: Summoned as archivist in the Ministry of Revenue; transferred to director of the Imperial Academy; promoted to erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as a Ministry of Revenue archivist, he became director of the Imperial Academy and rose to erudite.

sentences.zh: 時棟為祭酒，講學益詣精邃。

translations.literal: At that time Dong was libationer; their lectures grew ever more penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Dong was now libationer, and their joint instruction grew subtler still.

sentences.zh: 遷國子博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to national-university erudite.

sentences.zh: 丐外，添差通判臺州。

translations.literal: He begged an outside post and was given an additional assignment as vice prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking a provincial post, he received an additional assignment as vice prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 故事，守貳尚華侈，正月望，取燈民間，吏以白，文仲曰：“為吾然一燈足矣。

translations.literal: By custom the prefect and vice prefect still favored luxury; on the fifteenth of the first month they took lanterns from the populace; when the clerks reported this, Wenzhong said, "Light one lantern for me—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Custom held that prefect and vice still loved display; on the Lantern Festival clerks proposed seizing lamps from the people, but Wenzhong said: "One lamp for me will do."

sentences.zh: ”劭農東郊，守因欲泛湖，文仲即先馳歸。

translations.literal: When the vice prefect urged agriculture in the eastern suburbs, the prefect wished to go boating on the lake; Wenzhong galloped home ahead of him.
translations.idiomatic: When he led the spring plowing rite east of the city and the prefect meant to cruise the lake, Wenzhong rode back first.

sentences.zh: 添差通判揚州。

translations.literal: He was given an additional assignment as vice prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received an additional post as vice prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 牙契舊額歲為錢四萬緡，累政增至十六萬，開告訐以求羨。

translations.literal: The old deed-tax quota was forty thousand strings a year; successive administrations had raised it to one hundred sixty thousand, opening informers' suits to seek surpluses.
translations.idiomatic: Property-transfer tax had stood at forty thousand strings yearly; successive regimes had pushed it to one hundred sixty thousand, encouraging informers to pad the take.

sentences.zh: 文仲曰：“希賞以擾民，吾不為也。

translations.literal: Wenzhong said, "To court reward by harassing the people—that I will not do."
translations.idiomatic: He declared: "I will not trouble the people to win favor."

sentences.zh: ”卒增十八界一而已。

translations.literal: In the end he raised it by only one denomination of the eighteen-realm notes.
translations.idiomatic: He increased the levy by only one step on the paper-money scale.

sentences.zh: 制置使李庭芝檄主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Li Tingzhi ordered him to take charge of planning documents.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingzhi, coastal pacification commissioner, put him in charge of strategic papers.

sentences.zh: 時有沙田，使者欲舉行之，文仲力爭，以為：“事不可妄興，蓋與民之惠有限，不擾之惠無窮。

translations.literal: At the time there were sand flats; an envoy wished to launch reclamation; Wenzhong argued forcefully, saying, "Affairs must not be rashly undertaken; benefits given the people are finite, but the benefit of leaving them undisturbed is endless."
translations.idiomatic: Officials proposed reclaiming tidal sand flats; Wenzhong fought the plan: "Projects must not be launched lightly—measured favors to the people are limited; the favor of peace is inexhaustible."

sentences.zh: 江北風寒之地，民力竭矣，為利幾何，安忍重擾吾民乎！

translations.literal: "The north of the river is a cold land; popular strength is exhausted; how much profit would there be—how can we bear again to harass our people!"
translations.idiomatic: "North of the Yangtze the wind bites and the people are spent—what trifling gain could justify tormenting them again?"

sentences.zh: ”事遂不行。

translations.literal: The project was therefore not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The scheme was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 召為宗學博士。

translations.literal: He was summoned as erudite of the Imperial Clan Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as erudite of the imperial-clan academy.

sentences.zh: 郊祀，攝圜壇子階監察御史。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice he acted as supervising censor on the subsidiary tier of the Circular Altar.
translations.idiomatic: During the suburban rites he served as acting censor on the lower terrace of the round altar.

sentences.zh: 近輔兵變水患，輪對，言：“皇天眷命，垂四百年，天命久熟之餘，國脈癃老之候，此豈非一大喜懼之交乎？

translations.literal: With military mutiny and flooding near the capital, in his rotating audience he said, "Heaven's favoring mandate has lasted nearly four hundred years; after long ripening of the Mandate comes the symptom of a feeble national pulse—is this not a moment when great joy and great fear meet?"
translations.idiomatic: After mutiny and floods struck the capital approaches, he told the throne: "Heaven's mandate has favored us nearly four centuries; when the mandate has ripened long, the dynasty's pulse turns feeble—is this not the hour when exultation and terror cross?"

sentences.zh: 願陛下一初清明，自作主宰。

translations.literal: "I wish Your Majesty, at the very beginning, to be clear and bright and be your own master."
translations.idiomatic: "May Your Majesty, from this fresh start, keep a clear mind and rule in your own person."

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“春多沈陰，豈但麥秋之憂。

translations.literal: He also said, "Spring brings much overcast; this is not only a worry for the wheat harvest."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Spring lies heavy under cloud—concern runs deeper than the summer grain."

sentences.zh: 於時為《》，尤軫莧陸之慮。

translations.literal: At that season the hexagram was Guai (Breakthrough), and he was especially grieved by the omen of purslane in its lines.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes then showed Guai, Breakthrough—and he dwelt anxiously on the portent of purslane in its judgment.

sentences.zh: 天目則洪水發焉，蘇、湖則弄兵興焉。

translations.literal: At Tianmu, floods broke out; in Suzhou and Huzhou, armed disturbances arose.
translations.idiomatic: Floods burst from Tianmu; mutiny flared in Suzhou and Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 峨冠於於，而每見大夫之乏使；

translations.literal: High caps thronged in number, yet envoys among grand masters were ever scarce.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in lofty hats packed the halls, yet grand masters to dispatch were always few.

sentences.zh: 佩印累累，而常慮貪瀆之無厭。

translations.literal: Seals hung in strings, yet one constantly feared that greed and corruption would know no end.
translations.idiomatic: Seals clustered on sashes, yet corruption seemed never to end.

sentences.zh: 將習黃金橫帶之娛，兵疲赤籍掛虛之穴。

translations.literal: Generals would grow used to the pleasures of gold horizontal belts; troops were weary, and the red registers hung with empty names.
translations.idiomatic: Generals would settle into gold-belted ease while soldiers languished and muster rolls bloated with ghosts.

sentences.zh: 蚩蚩編氓，得以輕統府；

translations.literal: The common people in their masses could lightly defy commandery offices.
translations.idiomatic: Humble subjects dared treat prefectural authority lightly.

sentences.zh: 瑣瑣警遽，輒以憂朝廷。

translations.literal: Petty alarms constantly made the court anxious.
translations.idiomatic: Petty panics already shook the throne.

sentences.zh: 設不幸事有大於此者，國何賴焉？

translations.literal: "If misfortune should bring something greater than this, on whom would the state rely?"
translations.idiomatic: "If worse should come, whom can the realm lean on?"

sentences.zh: ”帝竦聽，顧問甚至。

translations.literal: The emperor listened with startled attention and questioned him at great length.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor listened, shaken, and questioned him at length.

sentences.zh: 遷太常丞，尋兼權倉部郎官，兼崇政殿說書，遷將作少監，又遷將作監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; soon concurrently acting director in the Granaries Bureau, and lecturer in the Hall of Lofty Government; transferred to vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, then director.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he soon doubled as acting granaries director and lecturer in the Hall of Lofty Government, then rose to vice and full director of palace works.

sentences.zh: 文仲在講筵，每以積誠感動，嘗進讀《春秋》，帝問五霸何以為三王罪人，文仲奏云：“齊桓公當王霸升降之會，而不能為向上事業，獨能開世變厲階。

translations.literal: In the lecture hall Wenzhong often moved others by accumulated sincerity; once, lecturing on the Spring and Autumn Annals, the emperor asked why the Five Hegemons were called criminals against the Three Kings; Wenzhong replied, "Duke Huan of Qi stood at the turning between kingship and hegemony yet could not pursue an upward course; he alone opened the age's change and a perilous stair."
translations.idiomatic: On the lecture dais Wenzhong often won hearts by sheer earnestness; reading the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was asked why the Five Hegemons were the Three Kings' offenders. He answered: "Duke Huan of Qi stood where kingship and hegemony met, yet chose not the higher path—he only opened the door to an age of decline."

sentences.zh: 臣考諸《春秋》，桓公初年多書‘人’，越二十年，伐楚定世子之功既成，然後書‘侯’之辭叠見，此所以為尊王抑伯之大法。

translations.literal: "Your servant has examined the Spring and Autumn Annals: in Duke Huan's early years the text often writes 'man'; after more than twenty years, once his campaigns against Chu and the securing of the heir were achieved, the word 'marquis' appears again and again—this is the great method of honoring the king and restraining hegemons."
translations.idiomatic: "In the Annals, Huan's early years call him 'man'; only after twenty years, when he had chastised Chu and fixed the succession, does 'marquis' recur—that is how the classic honors the king and curbs the hegemon."

sentences.zh: 然王豈徒尊哉？

translations.literal: "Yet was kingship honored for nothing?"
translations.idiomatic: "But was the king honored in name alone?"

sentences.zh: 蓋欲周王子孫率修文、武、成、康之法度，以扶持文、武、成、康之德澤，則王跡不熄，西周之美可尋，如此方副《春秋》尊王之意。

translations.literal: "It was rather that the Zhou royal house should lead its descendants to maintain the institutions of Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang, and uphold their beneficent rule—then the king's trace would not die and the beauty of the Western Zhou could be sought again; only thus does one fulfill the Spring and Autumn's intent to honor the king."
translations.idiomatic: "The point was that Zhou's sons should live by the laws of Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang and keep their grace alive—so the royal way would not gutter out and Western Zhou's splendor could return. Only that fulfills the Annals' call to honor the king."

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“先帝聖訓有曰：‘絲竹之亂耳，紅紫之眩目，良心善性，皆本有之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The late emperor's sacred instruction runs: 'Music confuses the ear, bright colors dazzle the eye—yet a good heart and nature are originally there.'"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Our late father taught: 'Pipe and string confuse the ear, crimson and purple dazzle the eye—yet conscience and humaneness are ours from the first.'"

sentences.zh: ’又曰：‘得聖賢心學之指要，本領端正，家傳世守，以是而君國子民，以是而祈天永命，以是而貽謀燕翼。

translations.literal: "He also said: 'Grasp the essentials of the sages' mind-learning, keep the root upright, hand it down through the family, and with it rule the realm and shepherd the people, pray to Heaven for enduring mandate, and bequeath counsel to posterity.'"
translations.idiomatic: "He also said: 'Hold the sages' heart-learning, keep the root straight, pass it down at home—so rule the people, so pray Heaven for long life, so leave counsel to those who come after.'"

sentences.zh: ’大哉先訓，朕朝夕服膺。

translations.literal: "Great is that former instruction; We wear it morning and evening."
translations.idiomatic: "Mighty is that teaching; We cherish it dawn to dusk."

sentences.zh: ”時帝以疾連不視朝，文仲奏：“聲色之事，若識得破，元無可好。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor, owing to illness, had long ceased to hold court; Wenzhong memorialized, "Matters of sound and color—once seen through, there is fundamentally nothing to love."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long absented himself from court through illness; Wenzhong said: "Sensual pleasures, once truly understood, hold no charm at all."

sentences.zh: ”帝斂容端拱久之。

translations.literal: The emperor composed his expression and sat upright in silence for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gathered his face and sat in formal silence a long while.

sentences.zh: 盛夏，建宗陽宮，壞徙民居，畿甸騷然。

translations.literal: In the height of summer the Zongyang Palace was built, demolishing and relocating common dwellings; the capital region was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: That midsummer they built the Zongyang Palace, tearing down neighborhoods to make incense courts; the capital approaches seethed.

sentences.zh: 文仲疏諫：“移閭閻之聚，為香火之庭，不得為善計矣。

translations.literal: Wenzhong remonstrated in a memorial: "To move the gathered lanes of the people and make a hall of incense is no good policy."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong protested in writing: "Uprooting whole neighborhoods for a temple court is no worthy plan."

sentences.zh: 陛下紹祖宗之位，豈以黃、老之居為輕重哉。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty inherits the throne of your ancestors—how can the dwellings of Huang-Lao weigh in the balance?"
translations.idiomatic: "You hold the seat of your forebears—surely a Daoist shrine cannot outweigh that trust."

sentences.zh: ”翼日面奏，益懇至，丞相賈似道怒曰：“楊文仲多言！

translations.literal: The next day he spoke face to face with still greater earnestness; Chancellor Jia Sidao said in anger, "Yang Wenzhong talks too much!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day he argued in person with still fiercer urgency; Chancellor Jia Sidao snapped: "Yang Wenzhong will not stop talking!"

sentences.zh: ”紹卿監以上薦人才，文仲薦陳存、呂折、鐘季玉等十有八人，名士二人，金華王柏、天臺車若水也。

translations.literal: When the Director of the Palace Domestic Service and above were to recommend talent, Wenzhong recommended Chen Cun, Lü Zhe, Zhong Jiyu, and eighteen others in all, among them two famous scholars—Wang Bo of Jinhua and Che Ruoshui of Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to recommend men of talent, he named Chen Cun, Lü Zhe, Zhong Jiyu, and eighteen others, including the celebrated Wang Bo of Jinhua and Che Ruoshui of Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 兼國子司業，兼侍立修註官。

translations.literal: Concurrently Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and attending reviser and annotator.
translations.idiomatic: He doubled as vice director of the directorate of education and as attending reviser.

sentences.zh: 又以救太學教諭彭成大迕似道，主管崇禧觀，出知衡州。

translations.literal: Again, because he had rescued Imperial Academy instructor Peng Chengda and thereby offended Sidao, he was made director of the Chongxi Observatory and sent out as prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had also shielded academy instructor Peng Chengda from Jia Sidao; for that he was parked at the Chongxi Observatory and exiled as prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 運餉有法而民不擾，以所當得米八千石立思濟倉。

translations.literal: He transported grain by rules that did not disturb the people and used eight thousand piculs of rice due him to establish the Siji Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He moved supplies efficiently without harassing the people and devoted eight thousand piculs of his stipend rice to found the Siji relief granary.

sentences.zh: 召為秘書少監，尋兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: Summoned as vice director of the Secretariat; soon concurrently lecturer in the Hall of Lofty Government.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as vice director of the secretariat, he soon lectured again in the Hall of Lofty Government.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞致仕，不許。

translations.literal: He begged retirement on grounds of illness; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Illness moved him to ask leave; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官，遷太常少卿兼國子司業，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: Concurrently compiler of the National History Institute and reviser of the Veritable Records Institute; transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with concurrent vice directorship of the Directorate of Education; transferred to Attendant of the Bureau of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently on the national history and veritable records staffs, became vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and of the directorate of education, then attendant of the bureau of attendants.

sentences.zh: 謝枋得，字君直，信州弋陽人也。

translations.literal: Xie Fangde, courtesy name Junzhi, was a native of Yiyang in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fangde, style name Junzhi, came from Yiyang in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為人豪爽。

translations.literal: In character he was bold and open.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-handed and forthright by nature.

sentences.zh: 每觀書，五行俱下，一覽終身不忘。

translations.literal: Whenever he read, he took in five lines at once and, once read, never forgot for life.
translations.idiomatic: He read five lines at a glance and never forgot what he had seen.

sentences.zh: 性好直言，一與人論古今治亂國家事，必掀髯抵幾，跳躍自奮，以忠義自任。

translations.literal: He loved to speak plainly; whenever he debated with others the rise and fall of states through the ages, he would tug his beard and strike the table, leap up in excitement, and take loyalty and righteousness as his charge.
translations.idiomatic: He loved blunt truth; debating the fortunes of dynasties past and present he would seize his beard, pound the table, spring to his feet, and bind himself to loyalty and duty.

sentences.zh: 徐霖稱其“如驚鶴摩霄，不事籠縶。

translations.literal: Xu Lin praised him as "like a startled crane brushing the sky, unwilling to be caged."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Lin said of him: "Like a crane startled into the clouds—he will not be penned."

sentences.zh: 寶祐中，舉進士，對策極攻丞相董槐與宦官董宋臣，意擢高第矣，及奏名，中乙科。

translations.literal: In the Baoyou era he passed the jinshi examination; in the policy essay he fiercely attacked Chancellor Dong Huai and the eunuch Dong Songchen; he expected a high placement, but when the names were announced he ranked in the second class.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoyou he took the jinshi; his policy essay savaged Chancellor Dong Huai and the eunuch Dong Songchen—he expected top honors, but the list placed him in the second class.

sentences.zh: 除撫州司戶參軍，即棄去。

translations.literal: He was made revenue assistant in Fuzhou and at once abandoned the post.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed revenue aide in Fuzhou, he walked away immediately.

sentences.zh: 明年復出，試教官，中兼經科，除教授建寧府。

translations.literal: The next year he came out again, tested as an instructor, passed the combined classics category, and was made professor of Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he tested as an instructor, won the combined-classics category, and was posted professor at Jianning.

sentences.zh: 未上，吳潛宣撫江東、西，辟差幹辦公事。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, Wu Qian, pacification commissioner of Jiangdong and Jiangxi, recruited him as a preparatory clerk on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reported, Wu Qian, pacifying Jiangdong and Jiangxi, drafted him as a staff clerk.

sentences.zh: 團結民兵，以扞饒、信、撫，科降錢米以給之。

translations.literal: He organized militia to defend Rao, Xin, and Fu, and levied grain and money to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered militia for Rao, Xin, and Fu and assessed grain and cash to feed them.

sentences.zh: 枋得說鄧、傳二社諸大家，得民兵萬餘人，守信州，暨兵退，朝廷核諸軍費，幾至不免。

translations.literal: Fangde persuaded the great clans of the Deng and Chuan communities and raised more than ten thousand militiamen; he held Xin Prefecture, and after the enemy withdrew the court audited the armies' expenses and he narrowly escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Fangde rallied the Deng and Chuan lineage heads and gathered ten thousand militia; he held Xinzhou, and when the troops withdrew the court audited war costs—he barely escaped penalty.

sentences.zh: 五年，彗星出東方，枋得考試建康，擿似道政事為問目，言：“兵必至，國必亡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year a comet appeared in the east; Fangde, examining candidates in Jiankang, made Jia Sidao's governance the topic of the examination and wrote, "War is certain to come; the state is certain to perish."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year a comet rose in the east; while examining students at Jiankang he set Jia Sidao's rule as the examination theme and wrote: "Armies will come; the dynasty will fall."

sentences.zh: ”漕使陸景思銜之，上其稿於似道，坐居鄉不法，起兵時冒破科降錢，且訕謗，追兩官，謫居興國軍。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Lu Jingsi bore a grudge and sent his draft to Sidao; he was convicted of unlawful conduct at home, of embezzling assessed grain when raising troops, and of slander; two ranks were stripped and he was banished to Xingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Lu Jingsi, resentful, forwarded the papers to Sidao; Fangde was found to have broken the law at home, to have misused relief grain when raising troops, and to have slandered officials—two ranks were taken and he was exiled to Xingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳三年，赦，放歸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianchun an amnesty was issued and he was released to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1267 an amnesty let him go home.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，呂文煥導大元兵東下鄂、黃、蘄、安慶、九江，凡其親友部曲皆誘下之，遂屯建康。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou, Lü Wenhuan guided the Great Yuan armies eastward through E, Huang, Qi, Anqing, and Jiujiang; all his kin, friends, and subordinates were induced to surrender, and they then encamped at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 Lü Wenhuan led the Yuan armies down the Yangtze through Ezhou, Huangzhou, Qizhou, Anqing, and Jiujiang; kinsmen, friends, and officers alike were lured to defect, and the host camped at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 枋得與呂師夔善，乃應詔上書，以一族保師夔可信，乞分沿江諸屯兵，以之為鎮撫使，使之行成，且願身至江州見文煥與議。

translations.literal: Fangde was on good terms with Lü Shiqiao. By imperial order he submitted a memorial, pledging his whole clan as guarantee that Shiqiao was trustworthy, and requesting that garrison troops along the river be divided and Shiqiao made Pacification Commissioner to conduct peace negotiations. He also wished to go in person to Jiangzhou to see Wen Huan and discuss matters.
translations.idiomatic: Fangde was on good terms with Lü Shiqiao. By imperial order he submitted a memorial, pledging his whole clan as guarantee that Shiqiao was trustworthy, and asking that garrison troops along the river be divided and Shiqiao made Pacification Commissioner to conduct peace negotiations. He also offered to go in person to Jiangzhou to see Wen Huan and discuss terms.

sentences.zh: 從之，使以沿江察訪使行，會文煥北歸，不及而反。

translations.literal: The court assented and sent him as River Circuit Investigating Commissioner. It happened that Wen Huan returned north, and he did not reach him in time and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: The court assented and sent him as River Circuit Investigating Commissioner. Wen Huan had already returned north, however, and Fangde failed to reach him in time and turned back.

sentences.zh: 以江東提刑、江西招諭使知信州。

translations.literal: He was made Judicial Intendant of Jiangdong, Pacification and Exhortation Commissioner of Jiangxi, and Prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Judicial Intendant of Jiangdong, Pacification and Exhortation Commissioner of Jiangxi, and prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，師夔與武萬戶分定江東地，枋得以兵逆之，使前鋒呼曰：“謝提刑來。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Shiqiao and Commander Wu divided and settled the lands of Jiangdong. Fangde opposed them with troops and had his vanguard call out, "Commissioner Xie has come."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, Shiqiao and Commander Wu divided and settled the lands of Jiangdong. Fangde opposed them with troops and had his vanguard call out, "Commissioner Xie has come."

sentences.zh: ”呂軍馳至，射之，矢及馬前。

translations.literal: Lü's army galloped up and shot at them; arrows reached before the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Lü's army galloped up and opened fire; arrows struck before their horses.

sentences.zh: 枋得走入安仁，調淮士張孝忠逆戰團湖坪，矢盡，孝忠揮雙刀擊殺百餘人。

translations.literal: Fangde fled into Anren and mobilized the Huai native Zhang Xiaozhong to meet the enemy in battle at Tuanhu Flat. When arrows were exhausted, Xiaozhong wielded twin blades and killed more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Fangde fled into Anren and mobilized the Huai native Zhang Xiaozhong to meet the enemy at Tuanhu Flat. When their arrows ran out, Xiaozhong wielded twin blades and killed more than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 前軍稍卻，後軍繞出孝忠後，眾驚潰，孝忠中流矢死。

translations.literal: The front army slightly retreated; the rear army circled behind Xiaozhong. The troops panicked and broke; Xiaozhong was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: The front line gave ground slightly; the rear line circled behind Xiaozhong. The troops panicked and broke; Xiaozhong was struck by a stray arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 馬奔歸，枋得坐敵樓見之，曰：“馬歸，孝忠敗矣。

translations.literal: Horses came galloping back. Fangde sat on the enemy tower and saw it, saying, "The horses return — Xiaozhong is defeated."
translations.idiomatic: Horses came galloping back. Fangde sat on the watchtower and saw them, saying, "The horses are returning — Xiaozhong is defeated."

sentences.zh: ”遂奔信州。

translations.literal: He thereupon fled to Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon fled to Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 師夔下安仁，進攻信州，不守。

translations.literal: Shiqiao descended on Anren and advanced to attack Xinzhou, which could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqiao descended on Anren and advanced to attack Xinzhou, which could not be held.

sentences.zh: 枋得乃變姓名，入建寧唐石山，轉茶阪，寓逆旅中，日麻衣躡屨，東鄉而哭，人不識之，以為被病也。

translations.literal: Fangde then changed his name, entered Tangshi Mountain in Jianning, turned onto Chaban, and lodged at an inn. Daily he wore hemp garments and trod in straw sandals, faced east and wept. People did not recognize him and thought he was ill.
translations.idiomatic: Fangde then changed his name, entered Tangshi Mountain in Jianning, turned onto Chaban, and lodged at an inn. Each day he wore hemp garments and straw sandals, faced east, and wept. No one recognized him; they thought he was ill.

sentences.zh: 已而去，賣卜建陽市中，有來卜者，惟取米屢而已，委以錢，率謝不取。

translations.literal: After a time he left and sold divinations in the market of Jianyang. When someone came for divination he would take only a few measures of rice; if money was offered, he invariably declined it.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he left and sold divinations in the market of Jianyang. When someone came for divination he would take only a few measures of rice; if money was offered, he invariably refused it.

sentences.zh: 其後人稍稍識之，多延至其家，使為弟子論學。

translations.literal: Afterwards people gradually recognized him and often invited him to their homes to lecture students on learning.
translations.idiomatic: Afterwards people gradually recognized him and often invited him to their homes to teach students.

sentences.zh: 天下既定，遂居閩中。

translations.literal: When all under Heaven was settled, he thereupon dwelt in Min.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was settled, he made his home in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 至元二十三年，集賢學士程文海薦宋臣二十二人，以枋得為首，辭不起。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan, Academician Cheng Wenhui recommended twenty-two Song subjects, with Fangde at their head. He declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1286, Academician Cheng Wenhui recommended twenty-two former Song subjects, with Fangde at their head. He declined and would not take office.

sentences.zh: 又明年，行省丞相忙兀臺將旨詔之，執手相勉勞。

translations.literal: In the following year, Chief Councillor of the Branch Secretariat Mangwutai brought an edict to summon him, took his hand, and exhorted and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Chief Councillor of the Branch Secretariat Mangwutai brought an edict to summon him, took his hand, and exhorted and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 枋得曰：“上有堯、舜，下有巢、由，枋得名姓不祥，不敢赴詔。

translations.literal: Fangde said, "Above there are Yao and Shun; below there are Chao and You. The name and surname Fangde are inauspicious — I dare not obey the summons."
translations.idiomatic: Fangde said, "Above there are Yao and Shun; below there are Chao and You. The name Fangde is inauspicious — I dare not obey the summons."

sentences.zh: ”丞相義之，不強也。

translations.literal: The chief councillor approved his righteousness and did not force him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillor approved his integrity and did not force him.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，福建行省參政管如德將旨如江南求人材，尚書留夢炎以枋得薦，枋得遺書夢炎曰：“江南無人材，求一瑕呂飴甥、程嬰、杵臼廝養卒，不可得也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Branch Secretariat Administrator Guan Rude of Fujian brought an edict to Jiangnan to seek men of talent. Minister Liu Mengyan recommended Fangde. Fangde sent Mengyan a letter saying, "Jiangnan has no men of talent — to seek one flawed nephew of Lü Yixu, one Cheng Ying, one mortar-and-pestle menial groom, cannot be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: In 1288, Branch Secretariat Administrator Guan Rude of Fujian brought an edict to Jiangnan to seek men of talent. Minister Liu Mengyan recommended Fangde. Fangde wrote to Mengyan, saying, "Jiangnan has no men of talent — you could not find even one flawed nephew of Lü Yixu, one Cheng Ying, or one mortar-and-pestle menial groom."

sentences.zh: 紂之亡也，以八百國之精兵，而不敢抗二子之正論，武王、太公凜凜無所容，急以興滅繼絕謝天下。

translations.literal: When Zhou died, though he had the elite troops of eight hundred states, he did not dare resist the upright discourse of two men. King Wu and Grand Duke Wang stood in awe with nowhere to turn, and urgently restored extinguished states and continued severed lines to apologize to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When King Zhou fell, though he had the elite troops of eight hundred states, he did not dare resist the upright remonstrance of two men. King Wu and the Grand Duke stood in awe with nowhere to turn, and urgently restored extinguished states and continued severed lines to apologize to the realm.

sentences.zh: 殷之後遂與周並立。

translations.literal: The descendants of Yin thereupon stood alongside Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The descendants of Yin thereupon stood alongside Zhou.

sentences.zh: 使三監、淮夷不叛，武庚必不死，殷命必不黜。

translations.literal: If the Three Overseers and the Huaiyi had not rebelled, Wugeng would certainly not have died and the mandate of Yin would certainly not have been removed.
translations.idiomatic: If the Three Overseers and the Huaiyi had not rebelled, Wugeng would certainly not have died and the mandate of Yin would certainly not have been removed.

sentences.zh: 夫女真之待二帝亦慘矣。

translations.literal: The Jurchens' treatment of the two emperors was also cruel.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens' treatment of the two emperors was cruel enough.

sentences.zh: 而我宋今年遣使祈請，明年遣使問安。

translations.literal: Yet our Song this year sent envoys to pray and request, and next year sent envoys to inquire after their health.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our Song sent envoys one year to pray and petition, and the next year sent envoys to inquire after their health.

sentences.zh: 王倫一市井無賴、狎邪小人，謂梓宮可還，太后可歸。

translations.literal: Wang Lun was a market-town scoundrel and debauched petty man who said the imperial coffin could be returned and the empress dowager could come home.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lun was a market-town scoundrel and debauched petty man who said the imperial coffin could be returned and the empress dowager could come home.

sentences.zh: 終則二事皆符其言。

translations.literal: In the end both matters matched his words.
translations.idiomatic: In the end both matters came to pass as he had said.

sentences.zh: 今一王倫且無之，則江南無人材可見也。

translations.literal: Today not even one Wang Lun exists — then no talent in Jiangnan is to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Today not even one Wang Lun exists — so what talent in Jiangnan can there be to see?

sentences.zh: 今吾年六十餘矣，所欠一死耳，豈復有它誌哉！

translations.literal: Today I am more than sixty years old; all that remains is one death — how could I have any other ambition!
translations.idiomatic: Today I am more than sixty years old; all that remains is one death — how could I have any other ambition!

sentences.zh: ”終不行。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not go.

sentences.zh: 郭少師從瀛國公入朝，既而南歸，與枋得道時事，曰：“大元本無意江南，屢遣使使頓兵，令毋深入，待還歲幣即議和，無枉害生靈也。

translations.literal: Guo Shaoshi followed Duke Ying of Guo to court; afterward he returned south and told Fangde the affairs of the time, saying, "The Great Yuan originally had no intention toward Jiangnan. Repeatedly they sent envoys to halt the army and ordered that it not advance deeply, waiting until the annual tribute was returned and then discussing peace, so as not to harm the people in vain."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shaoshi had followed Duke Ying of Guo to court at the Yuan capital; afterward he returned south and told Fangde how things stood, saying, "The Great Yuan originally had no intention toward Jiangnan. Repeatedly they sent envoys to halt the army and ordered that it not advance deeply, waiting until the annual tribute was returned and then discussing peace, so as not to harm the people in vain."

sentences.zh: 張宴然上書乞斂兵從和，上即可之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanran submitted a memorial requesting that troops be gathered in and peace followed; the sovereign immediately approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanran submitted a memorial requesting that troops be gathered in and peace pursued; the sovereign immediately approved it.

sentences.zh: 兵交二年，無一介行李之事，乃挈數百年宗社而降。

translations.literal: Armies clashed for two years without a single bag of luggage being sent, yet they then surrendered the altars of state of several hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Armies clashed for two years without a single bag of tribute being sent, yet the court then surrendered the altars of state of several hundred years.

sentences.zh: ”因相與痛哭。

translations.literal: They thereupon wept together.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon wept together.

sentences.zh: 福建行省參政魏天祐見時方以求材為急，欲薦枋得為功，使其友趙孟<辶卸>來言，枋得罵曰：“天祐仕閩，無毫髮推廣德意，反起銀冶病民，顧以我輩飾好邪？

translations.literal: Branch Secretariat Administrator Wei Tianyou of Fujian saw that the time urgently sought talent and wished to recommend Fangde for merit. He sent his friend Zhao Mengfu to speak with him. Fangde cursed and said, "Tianyou served in Min without advancing virtue in the slightest hair, yet raised silver smelting to afflict the people — and now he would use us to adorn his goodness?"
translations.idiomatic: Branch Secretariat Administrator Wei Tianyou of Fujian saw that the court urgently sought talent and wished to recommend Fangde for merit. He sent his friend Zhao Mengfu to speak with him. Fangde cursed and said, "Tianyou served in Fujian without advancing virtue in the slightest, yet raised silver smelting to afflict the people — and now he would use us to adorn his reputation?"

sentences.zh: ”及見天祐，又傲岸不為禮，與之言，坐而不對。

translations.literal: When he met Tianyou he was again proud and gave no courtesy; when Tianyou spoke to him, he sat and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Tianyou he was again proud and gave no courtesy; when Tianyou spoke to him, he sat in silence and would not reply.

sentences.zh: 天祐怒，強之而北。

translations.literal: Tianyou was enraged and forced him north.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou was enraged and forced him north.

sentences.zh: 枋得即日食菜果。

translations.literal: Fangde that very day ate only vegetables and fruit.
translations.idiomatic: That very day Fangde began eating only vegetables and fruit.

sentences.zh: 二十六年四月，至京師，問謝太后欑所及瀛國所在，再拜慟哭。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-sixth year he reached the capital, inquired after the place where Empress Dowager Xie's coffin lay and where Duke Ying of Guo was, bowed twice, and wept in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: In April of 1289 he reached the capital, inquired after the place where Empress Dowager Xie's coffin lay and where Duke Ying of Guo was, bowed twice, and wept in anguish.

sentences.zh: 已而病，遷憫忠寺，見壁間《曹娥碑》，泣曰：“小女子猶爾，吾豈不汝若哉！

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill and was moved to the Minzhong Temple. Seeing the "Stele of Cao E" on the wall, he wept and said, "Even a little girl was thus — how could I not be like you!"
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill and was moved to the Minzhong Temple. Seeing the "Stele of Cao E" on the wall, he wept and said, "Even a little girl did as much — how could I not do the same!"

sentences.zh: ”留夢炎使醫持藥雜米飲進之，枋得怒曰：“吾欲死，汝乃欲生我邪？

translations.literal: Liu Mengyan had a physician bring medicine mixed into rice gruel to feed him. Fangde angrily said, "I wish to die — do you wish to keep me alive?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mengyan had a physician bring medicine mixed into rice gruel to feed him. Fangde angrily said, "I wish to die — do you mean to keep me alive?"

sentences.zh: ”棄之於地，終不食而死。

translations.literal: He cast it on the ground and in the end refused to eat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He cast it on the ground and in the end refused to eat and died.

sentences.zh: 伯父徽明以特奏恩為當陽尉，攝縣事，時天基節上壽，大元兵奄至，徽明出兵戰死，二子趨進抱父屍，亦死。

translations.literal: His uncle Huiming, through special memorial grace, was Commandant of Dangyang and acted in county affairs. At the time of the Tianji Festival celebrating longevity, Great Yuan troops suddenly arrived. Huiming led troops out and died in battle; his two sons rushed forward and embraced their father's corpse and also died.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Huiming, through special memorial grace, was commandant of Dangyang and acted in county affairs. At the Tianji Festival celebrating longevity, Yuan troops suddenly arrived. Huiming led troops out and died in battle; his two sons rushed forward, embraced their father's corpse, and also died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：劉應龍不附賈似道，馮去非不附丁大全，潘方論皇子竑事，坎壈以終。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Liu Yinglong did not attach himself to Jia Sidao; Feng Qufei did not attach himself to Ding Daquan; Pan Fang spoke on the affair of Prince Yi and ended in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment says: Liu Yinglong would not attach himself to Jia Sidao; Feng Qufei would not attach himself to Ding Daquan; Pan Fang spoke on the affair of Prince Yi and ended in hardship.

sentences.zh: 洪芹訟吳潛，偉哉。

translations.literal: Hong Qin impeached Wu Qian — how grand!
translations.idiomatic: Hong Qin impeached Wu Qian — magnificent!

sentences.zh: 趙景緯。

translations.literal: Zhao Jingwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jingwei.

sentences.zh: 醇儒也，而無躁競之心。

translations.literal: A pure Confucian, yet without a restless, contentious heart.
translations.idiomatic: A pure Confucian, without a restless, contentious heart.

sentences.zh: 徐霖進則直言於朝，退則講道於裏。

translations.literal: Xu Lin, in advancing, spoke frankly at court; in retiring, lectured on the Way in his village.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Lin spoke frankly at court when he advanced and lectured on the Way in his village when he retired.

sentences.zh: 徐宗仁國亡與亡，異乎懷二心以事其君者也。

translations.literal: Xu Zongren perished when the state perished — different from those who harbored two hearts in serving their ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zongren perished when the state perished — unlike those who harbored divided loyalties in serving their ruler.

sentences.zh: 危昭德經筵進對之言，悉載諸故史。

translations.literal: Wei Zhaode's words in advancing to audience at the Classics Lectures are all recorded in the former histories.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaode's words in audience at the Classics Lectures are all recorded in the former histories.

sentences.zh: 陳塏能以意氣感人，楊文仲當搶攘之時，猶能薦士，謝枋得嵚崎以全臣節，皆宋末之卓然者也。

translations.literal: Chen Kai could move people by spirit and resolve; Yang Wenzhong, in a time of turmoil, could still recommend scholars; Xie Fangde, rugged and steep, preserved his integrity as a minister — all were outstanding men of the late Song.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kai could move people by spirit and resolve; Yang Wenzhong, in a time of turmoil, could still recommend scholars; Xie Fangde, rugged and unyielding, preserved his integrity as a minister — all were outstanding men of the late Song.
